Official YouTube page for news and updates from Ranking Member Lindsey Graham (R-SC) and the Republican members of the Senate Budget Committee.

On Twitter: http://twitter.com/BudgetGOP

2.title: Senate Budget Democrats
2.description: Fighting for an economy that puts workers and families first. The latest news from Ranking Member Sen. Jeff Merkley and Senate Budget Committee Dems.

1.title: Graham Calls Out Manchin-Schumer Bill for Not Addressing Inflation
1.description: WASHINGTON – Senate Budget Committee Ranking Member Lindsey Graham (R-South Carolina) today called out the Manchin-Schumer spending bill for not addressing inflation.  Graham noted that the Congressional Budget Office this week found that the Inflation Reduction Act will have “negligible effect” on inflation this year and may actually cause inflation to rise in 2023.

9.title: Senate, House Budget Committees Hold Press Conference on Democrats' Reckless Tax and Spend Bill
9.description: Top Republicans on Senate, House Budget Committees hold press conference on Democrats' Reckless Tax and Spend Bill.

10.title: VIDEO - Sen. Lindsey Graham reacts to Senate's approval of debt ceiling hike

20.title: Hearing on CBO’s Updated Budget Outlook
20.description: The Senate Budget Committee will hold a hearing to consider the Congressional Budget Office’s (CBO) updated budget outlook at 2:30pm on Wednesday, September 23, 2020 in the Dirksen Senate Office Building Room 608. Testifying will be Dr. Phillip Swagel, Director of the Congressional Budget Office.

21.title: Do Debt and Deficits Matter?
21.description: Do debt and deficits matter? Budget Committee Chairman Mike Enzi asks the Director of the Congressional Budget Office.

22.title: Enzi: While Congress Remains Focused on Pandemic,It Must Also Plan to Address Debt
22.description: During a hearing today on the Congressional Budget Office’s (CBO) recently released updated budget outlook, Senate Budget Committee Chairman Mike Enzi (R-WY) said while Congress remains focused on the pandemic facing the country, it must begin to address the national debt.

23.title: Committee Approves Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen Federal Financial Management
23.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee today approved Senate Budget Committee Chairman Mike Enzi (R-WY) and Senator Mark Warner’s legislation (D-VA) to strengthen federal financial management. The bill would update the Chief Financial Officers (CFO) Act of 1990, which created a new foundation for federal financial management. The law established a financial management leadership structure, provided for long-range planning, and required audited financial statements.

24.title: Budget Chairman Enzi Calls on Congress to Spend Responsibly on Next Pandemic Bill

25.title: Enzi Fights to Make Parks Legislation Fiscally Responsible
25.description: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Mike Enzi (R-WY) today raised a budget point of order under the Senate’s pay-as-you-go (PAYGO) rule against the Great American Outdoors Act, which would increase the deficit by more than $17 billion over the next 10 years.

26.title: Chairman Enzi: It’s time to fix our national parks, but we must do so responsibly

27.title: Bipartisan Bill Would Strengthen Federal Financial Management
27.description: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Mike Enzi (R-WY) this week introduced bipartisan legislation to strengthen federal financial management by updating the Chief Financial Officers (CFO) Act of 1990.

28.title: Chairman Enzi's Statement On President’s FY 2021 Budget Proposal
28.description:
Senator Mike Enzi (R-WY), Chairman of the Senate Budget Committee, issued the following statement today on the President’s fiscal year 2021 budget proposal:

“Presidents’ budgets are a reflection of Administration priorities, but in the end, they are just a list of suggestions, as the power of the purse rests with Congress,” said Chairman Enzi.  “Bipartisan consensus will be necessary to bring our debt and deficits under control.  I hope to work with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to put our country on a more sustainable fiscal course.”

29.title: Enzi Highlights Historic Bipartisan Budget Reforms
29.description: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Mike Enzi (R-WY) this week highlighted historic bipartisan budget process reform legislation recently approved by the Committee that would provide a more orderly and deliberative budget process focused on long-term fiscal planning.

30.title: Chairman Enzi: Pension Bailout Will Leave Taxpayers Holding the Fiscal Bag
30.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. – During a speech on the floor of the United States Senate, Budget Committee Chairman Mike Enzi (R-WY) warned that a House of Representatives-passed bill, the Rehabilitation for Multiemployer Plans Act of 2019, would bail out some of the worst-funded multiemployer plans at taxpayers’ expense.

31.title: October 2019 Scorekeeping Report
31.description: Today, Senate Budget Committee Chairman Mike Enzi (R-WY) announced the release of the October 2019 Senate scorekeeping report.  That report tracks the budgetary impact of legislation approved by Congress against the deemed budgetary numbers included in the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2019.  The Congressional Budget Act of 1974 requires the Chairmen of the House and Senate Budget Committees to provide members of Congress with regular updates on the budgetary effects of congressional action.

32.title: Enzi: America’s Fiscal Path is Unsustainable
32.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. – During a speech on the floor of the Senate, Budget Committee Chairman Mike Enzi (R-WY) today continued to raise alarm bells that America’s current fiscal course is unsustainable.  Enzi noted that in the first 11 months of the fiscal year, federal revenue increased by 3 percent compared to the same period last year, while spending increased by 7 percent.

33.title: Enzi Unveils Ideas to Fix the #BrokenBudget Process

34.title: Surging Federal Debt Puts Nation at Risk of Fiscal Crisis
34.description: During a speech today on the floor of the Senate, U.S. Senator Mike Enzi, R-Wyo., chairman of the Senate Budget Committee, called attention to the federal government’s unsustainable fiscal outlook and noted that a Congressional Budget Office report released this week on the long-term budget outlook projected that our surging federal debt is putting the nation at risk of a “fiscal crisis."

35.title: Chairman Enzi: Budget Process Reform Efforts Will Continue
35.description: During a speech on the floor of the United States Senate, Senator Mike Enzi (R-WY), Chairman of the Senate Budget Committee, today outlined his plans to begin fixing the broken budget and appropriations process in the new Congress

37.title: A Better Budget and a Better Way

38.title: Budget Process Reform - Senate Perspectives
38.description: Earlier this summer, Senate Budget Committee Chairman Mike Enzi put forward a set of budget process reform recommendations. Chairman Enzi will kick off the event with a keynote followed by a panel of experts that will discuss Enzi's recommendations in the areas of Senate budget procedures, biennial budgeting, a budget concepts commission, and portfolio budgeting.  Both the Senate and House Budget Committees held hearings and showed interest in moving forward with legislation to reform the budget process.

39.title: Learn More About America's Broken Budget Process

40.title: 2016 Fiscal Summit
40.description:
Senator Mike Enzi (R-WY), Chairman of the Senate Budget Committee, offered some ideas to fix America's broken budget process at the 2016 Fiscal Summit, sponsored by the Peter G. Peterson Foundation.

http://bit.ly/1Ts6PXG

41.title: Enzi: Congress Fails To Do Its Job By Not Balancing The Budget
41.description: JULY 6, WASHINGTON--In a speech on the Senate floor today, Sen. Michael Enzi urged the President and Senate Democrats to take meaningful action on the budget. He stated, "While Democrats continue to ignore the problem, Republicans look for solutions." Enzi also noted that It would be irresponsible for the Senate to increase the debt ceiling without putting in place serious measures to curb wasteful Washington spending.

42.title: Senate Approves Far-Reaching Obamacare Repeal
42.description: The United States Senate today passed the most comprehensive and far-reaching repeal of Obamacare possible.  The House of Representatives is expected take up and pass the Senate approved version shortly, which would send repeal legislation to the President for the first time in his tenure.

43.title: From Broken Promises to Better Care
43.description: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Mike Enzi (R-WY) today noted that Americans are ready to move past Obamacare’s broken promises to better health care as the U.S. Senate opened debate on repealing the president’s health care law as part of the budget reconciliation process.

44.title: In First Six months, Senate is Back to Work with a Balanced Budget
44.description: In first six months, the U.S. Senate is back to work for the American people with a Balanced Budget.

45.title: Congress approves first 10 Year balanced budget since 2001

46.title: Senate Begins Debate on Balanced Budget to Boost National Defense and Economic Growth

47.title: Senator Enzi speaking on the budget at the Ohio Clock Press Conference 03 24 2015

48.title: Sessions: Grow The Economy—Not The Government

49.title: Sessions: Will Any Senate Democrats Agree To Balance The Federal Budget?

50.title: Sessions Delivers Remarks Previewing Murray Budget Mark-Up And GOP Reform Agenda
50.description:
WASHINGTON, March 9--Speaking on behalf of his Republican colleagues in Congress, Sen. Sessions delivered the weekly GOP address today. Sessions laid out a vision for growing the economy, not the government, and said that "we have a moral duty to balance the federal budget."

Sessions went on: "Government has never been bigger or more out of control. They say there is no problem with waste, fraud, and abuse; they say the problem is you; they say you are not sending them enough money; they say they have wisely spent every penny. So, you must just send them more. And, if you don't? Well, they won't stop spending, they'll just borrow more. These destructive policies cannot continue. We are at the breaking point."

51.title: Sessions Opens Debate In Opposition Of Jack Lew Nomination
51.description: WASHINGTON, February 27--In the first of several remarks he made on the Senate floor today, Sen. Sessions laid out the case against voting to confirm Jack Lew to be Treasury Secretary.

52.title: Sessions: Independent Gov't Auditor Reveals Obamacare Will Add $6.2T To Long-Term Debt
52.description: WASHINGTON, February 26--At a Budget Committee hearing today, Ranking Member Sessions announced the results of a new Government Accountability Office report on the long-term deficit impact of the President's health law. The results are shocking: over the next 75 years, the law will add $6.2 trillion to the deficit in present value terms—not including the interest costs associated with the additional borrowing. This proves that President Obama's claim that he would "not sign a plan that adds one dime to our deficits—either now or in the future" were false.

53.title: Republicans Lay Out Moral Case For Welfare Reform
53.description: WASHINGTON, February 14—At a Budget Committee hearing yesterday, Sen. Sessions, other GOP Senators, and the panel of witnesses discussed the importance of crafting safety net policies that allow people to be able to take care of themselves and their families.

54.title: Sessions Replies To Murray Attack: Your Policies Hurting Poor, Not Ours
54.description: WASHINGTON, February 12--In the first Budget Committee hearing of the 113th Congress, Sen. Sessions delivered an opening statement in which he forcefully confronted the rhetoric from President Obama and Democrat leaders. Sessions stated: "I resent the fact that people suggest that those of us who have a different view of how to help poor people somehow don't care about them."

55.title: Lew Under Scrutiny For Misleading Congress
55.description: WASHINGTON, February 11--Tonight on "Special Report," Carl Cameron addressed some of the controversies surrounding Jack Lew's nomination to be Treasury Secretary.

56.title: CNN: Lew Faces 'The Most Serious Of Accusations'
56.description: WASHINGTON, February 5--Last night, CNN's "The Situation Room" discussed a new controversy surrounding Jack Lew's nomination to be Treasury Secretary.

57.title: Highlights: Sessions Pressures Senate's Dem Majority To Follow Law, Produce Budget
57.description: A compilation of clips from Ranking Member Sessions' floor speeches over the past year, as part of his effort to compel the Senate's Democratic majority to comply with the law and produce a budget.

58.title: Sessions: Jack Lew Misled Congress And Country With Repeated False Statements
58.description: WASHINGTON, January 23-- Today on the Senate floor, Sessions' discussed his opposition to Jack Lew's nomination to be Secretary of the Treasury, including Lew's coordinated effort to mislead Congress and the country about the fiscal impact of the President's budgets.

59.title: Varney Discusses 'Astonishing' Report: Welfare Spending To Surge 80% Over Next Decade

60.title: On Greta, Sessions Details Lew's History Of False Statements
60.description: WASHINGTON, January 11--Appearing on Fox's "On the Record" last night, Sen. Sessions outlined his opposition to Jack Lew's nomination to be Treasury Secretary. Sessions explained that when Lew testified before the Budget Committee less than two years ago, he made repeated false and misleading statements about what effect President Obama's budget would have on our debt. Sessions gave Lew multiple opportunities to correct the record, but he continued to insist that the President's budget would put the nation where we would "not be adding to the debt anymore." In fact, the budget in question would have added $13 trillion to the debt--according to the Administration's own numbers (http://1.usa.gov/11mSHEK).

61.title: Sessions Discusses Opposition To Lew Nomination On CNBC
61.description: WASHINGTON, January 10—This morning on CNBC, Sen. Sessions discussed Lew's appearance before Congress while he was serving as the President's budget director. Lew continued to insist that President Obama's budget would not add to the debt of the United States.

62.title: Sessions Discusses Opposition To Lew Nomination On CNN

63.title: On Kudlow, Sessions Discusses Growing Push To Condition Debt Increase On Senate Budget Compliance
63.description: WASHINGTON, January 9—Last night on "The Kudlow Report," Sen. Sessions discussed  the new push for any increase in the debt ceiling to be conditioned on the Senate passage of a budget plan. Such a proposal would ensure that any additional debt incurred on behalf of the American people would be tied to a concrete financial plan for how that money would be used.

64.title: Sessions Spars With CNN Host Over Need For Federal Budget

65.title: 'Special Report' Interviews Sessions On Food Stamp, Welfare Reform Efforts
65.description: WASHINGTON, December 13- Last night 'Special Report' ran a segment on food stamps and discussed Sen. Sessions' efforts to make food stamps a part of the fiscal cliff negotiations.

66.title: USDA Secretary Vilsack Stiffs Congressional Inquiry On Controversial Food Stamp Promotions
66.description: Budget Ranking Member Jeff Sessions addressed the record increase in food stamp enrollment and the failure of Agriculture Secretary Tom Vilsack to respond to a Congressional inquiry concerning USDA's promotions to surge food stamp enrollment among those who insist they don't need benefits.

67.title: Welfare Spending Equals $168 Per Day For Every Household In Poverty

68.title: Former Obama Advisor: Transparency In Fiscal Talks 'Not Good For The Negotiation'
68.description: WASHINGTON, December 10--On CNN's "Starting Point" last week, former Obama advisor Kenneth Baer disputed the notion that the public has a right to know what is being discussed in the secret fiscal talks between President Obama and Speaker John Boehner.

69.title: Sessions: President's Fiscal 'Plan' Would Result In Nearly $9T In New Debt
69.description: WASHINGTON, December 6—Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today to debunk the Administration's repeated claims that its fiscal "plan" would make our debt "stable and sustainable." In fact, because it increases spending by a trillion dollars, the nation would still accumulate almost $9 trillion in gross debt over the next 10 years.

70.title: Sessions: Secret Talks Haven't Worked For Two Years, 'Violate Principle Of American Gov't'
70.description: WASHINGTON, December 4—Greta Van Susteren interviewed Ranking Member Sessions regarding the secret fiscal negotiations and the Senator's belief that instead of pursuing more unsuccessful secret talks the process should be moved out of the shadows.

71.title: Sessions: White House Keeps Plans Secret To Conceal Massive Spending
71.description: WASHINGTON, November 30--In his remarks on the Senate floor today, Ranking Member Sessions said that the White House is keeping its fiscal plan secret in order to conceal the President's planned increase in spending.

72.title: Sessions: Why Aren't Reforms Being Discussed For Largest Portion Of Budget?
72.description:
WASHINGTON, November 29—In his remarks on the Senate floor today, Sen. Sessions drew attention to the fact that welfare spending now represents the largest component of the federal budget—more than Medicare, Social Security, or defense. Such spending is up about 30 percent since the President took office, and would see another 30 percent increase under his budget plan. Total spending on federal welfare reached approximately $1 trillion in 2011.

To view Sessions' earlier statement about how modest changes to welfare in the United States—including improved standards and work requirements—could yield $1 trillion in savings over 10 years, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/11547v5

73.title: Sessions Calls For Moving Secret Fiscal Negotiations 'Out Of The Shadows'
73.description: WASHINGTON, November 29—Sen. Sessions delivered remarks on the Senate floor today about the secret, year-end fiscal negotiations. To read his full remarks, please click here: 1.usa.gov/V6kQbc

74.title: America's Newsroom Interview With Senator Sessions On Need for Open Process
74.description: WASHINGTON, November 16—This morning on "America's Newsroom," Sen. Sessions discussed the  fiscal cliff and the need for the year-end negotiations to be conducted in a public, transparent manner.

75.title: As White House Talks Begin, Sessions Warns Against Another Secret Deal Produced At 11th Hour
75.description: WASHINGTON, November 16—This morning on "Starting Point" with Soledad O'Brien, Sen. Sessions discussed the so-called fiscal cliff, the combination of expiring tax rates and automatic spending cuts that are scheduled to take effect in January, disproportionately hitting defense spending. Sessions cautioned that another last-minute deal, rushed to passage under threat of crisis, is the likely result of continued secret negotiations. He said that Congress ought to finally debate these issues in the light of day so that members of the public have an opportunity to weigh in, learn the details, and know where their representatives stand.

76.title: Sessions Draws Attention To Broken Senate Process, Refusal Of Majority To Allow Votes Or Amendments
76.description: WASHINGTON, November 16—In a speech on the Senate floor yesterday, Sen. Sessions said he was "disappointed" that the upper chamber was not dealing with any of the important issues facing the nation. After a month-long recess during September, the Senate returned for three days this week only to go into recess again for another week. Although year-end action is necessary on taxes, the national defense bill, and automatic spending cuts, the Senate has yet to consider any legislation to confront these pressing issues, and the Senate Majority Leader has threatened not to allow members to offer amendments if and when the bills are considered.

77.title: Steve Forbes Discusses Welfare, Government Dependence, And Economic Uncertainty
77.description: WASHINGTON, October 25—On America's Newsroom this morning, Forbes magazine editor-in-chief Steve Forbes addressed recent figures about welfare, poverty, and government dependence in America. As the on-screen graphics indicate, food stamp usage has nearly tripled over the past decade, and roughly 1 in 3 Americans now participate in at least one means-tested federal welfare program. Total spending on such programs reached approximately $1 trillion in 2011 alone, more than the nation spends on Social Security, Medicare, or national defense.

78.title: O'Reilly Discusses New CRS Report On Record Federal Welfare Spending
78.description:
WASHINGTON, October 25—On the O'Reilly Factor last week, Bill O'Reilly discussed a new report from the Congressional Research Service, requested by Ranking Member Sessions, that found that welfare spending now makes up the largest portion of the federal budget—more than Social Security, Medicare, or national defense. In FY 2011 alone, the federal government spent $746 billion on cash aid, nutritional support, free medical care, and other benefit programs for low-income individuals. State spending on these same federal programs added another $283 billion, bringing total welfare spending in the United States to more than $1 trillion.

To view additional information about the CRS report, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/QwD1p9

79.title: Huckabee Praises Sessions' Efforts On Welfare Reform
79.description: WASHINGTON, October 25—Gov. Mike Huckabee recently discussed new figures from the Congressional Research Service about total spending on federal welfare programs, and praised Sen. Sessions' efforts in calling for a return to the principles of the 1996 welfare reform. To view additional information about the CRS report, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/QwD1p9

80.title: Sessions Delivers Weekly GOP Address, 9/22/12
80.description:
Ranking Member Sessions delivered the Weekly Republican Address and addressed the colossal spending in Washington: "American people see the financial chaos.  They know it must stop. They know their families are at risk.  And that their country is in danger."  In his remarks, Sessions provided data from the President's own budget to illustrate how it would add $11 trillion to the nation's debt, explaining, "For the President to say his plan will pay down the debt is one of the greatest financial misrepresentations ever made to the American people."

Sessions also discussed the decision of the Senate's Democrat Majority to adjourn having failed to pass a single spending bill, the defense authorization bill, or -- for three straight years -- a legally required budget.

In closing his remarks, Sessions outlined a "better way forward":

"We believe in growing the economy, not the bureaucracy.  We believe in helping more people live good and prosperous lives.  We believe in preventing the safety net from becoming a restraint.  We believe in lifting people onto the employment rolls instead of leaving them on the welfare rolls.  And we believe that compassion should not be defined by much money the government spends on poverty but how many people we can help rise out of poverty."

81.title: 'National Disgrace': Dems To Adjourn Senate With No Budget Plan For 3rd Year
81.description: WASHINGTON, September 20--A number of Republican Senators joined together on the Senate floor today to discuss the three-year failure of President Obama and the Senate's Democrat majority to offer any solutions to the nation's dangerously unsustainable debt.

82.title: Thune: With No Budget Of Their Own, Senate Dems Have No Standing To Criticize House Plan
82.description: WASHINGTON, September 13--Senate Republican Conference Chairman John Thune (SD) took to the Senate floor today to point out the hypocrisy of the chamber's Democrat majority in criticizing the House-passed Republican budget at a time when they have not produced any budget of their own in more than 1,200 days.

83.title: Senators: As Clock Ticks, Democrat Majority Refuses To Address Budget Or Looming Defense Cuts
83.description:
WASHINGTON, September 13—Sen. Sessions joined Sens. John Thune, John McCain, and Kelly Ayotte today on the Senate floor today to discuss several items that the Senate's Democrat majority has yet to address as Congress prepares to recess ahead of the November elections.

Among the outstanding items are: automatic sequestration cuts scheduled to take effect on January 2, any budget or appropriations bills, and the defense authorization bill.

Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid has said the chamber is unlikely to take up any individual spending bills this year (the House of Representatives has passed 7 so far), and this year will mark the first time in over 50 years that the Senate has failed to pass a defense authorization bill to lay out the spending and priorities of the Defense Department.

Meanwhile, it has been 1,233 days since the Senate's Democrat majority has adopted any budget plan at all.

84.title: Food Stamp Enrollment Reaches Record 46.7 Million
84.description: WASHINGTON, September 5--Newly available FNS data (http://1.usa.gov/5a0PbY) shows that food stamp enrollment climbed to nearly 46.7 million in June. Taking all welfare programs into account (including only means-tested benefits, not entitlements like Medicare or Social Security), 107 million Americans now receive some form of federal welfare, according to Census data (http://1.usa.gov/NfhKOV).

85.title: Improper Tax Payments To Illegals Quadruples, But Reid Blocks Fix
85.description: WASHINGTON, August 23--This morning on "America's Newsroom," host Bill Hemmer and the Daily Caller's Caroline May discussed a new Budget Committee finding about improper payments to illegal aliens under the Additional Child Tax Credit. The Treasury Department's own Inspector General found that these payments equaled $4 billion in 2010 (the last year for which data is available), and extrapolations suggest that amount will reach $7.4 billion this year.

86.title: Special Report: DHS, State Dept Failing To Comply With Committees' Welfare Oversight Letter
86.description: WASHINGTON, August 22--Last night on FOX News, Special Report aired a segment on the oversight letter from the Budget, Judiciary, Finance, and Agriculture Committees to Homeland Security Secretary Janet Napolitano and State Department Secretary Hillary Clinton. In their letter, Ranking Members Sessions, Grassley, Hatch, and Roberts asked the Secretaries to explain why the legal requirement that potential immigrants and visa applicants not be welfare-reliant has been effectively nullified. This requirement is set forth in section 212 of the Immigration and Nationality Act, and states that "An alien who... is likely at any time to become a public charge is inadmissible."

87.title: Special Report On Increase In Govt Dependency: 100M Now On Some Form Of Federal Welfare
87.description:
WASHINGTON, August 10--This evening on "Special Report with Bret Baier," correspondent Jim Angle examined the emergence of welfare reform as an issue this year, including the recent finding by the Senate Budget Committee that more than 100 million people in the U.S. are receiving some form of means-tested federal welfare benefit.

Note: This calculation includes legal immigrants, and does not count participation in either Social Security or Medicare.

88.title: O'Reilly Addresses Historic Growth In Federal Welfare
88.description: WASHINGTON, August 10--Last night on the O'Reilly Factor, Bill O'Reilly discussed the growth in welfare use in the United States, noting that more than 100 million people in the country now receive some form of federal welfare benefit. To view the Senate Budget Committee Republican staff's chart showing the growth in welfare use since 2009, click here: http://1.usa.gov/ItoDcB

89.title: Senators Demand Answers From Clinton, Napolitano On Removal Of Welfare Requirements For Immigrants
89.description: WASHINGTON, August 7--On America Live, Robert Rector, Heritage Foundation Senior Fellow, discussed the letter Ranking Members Jeff Sessions, Chuck Grassley, Orrin Hatch, and Pat Roberts sent to Department of Homeland Security Secretary Janet Napolitano and State Department Secretary Hillary Clinton. In their letter, the Senators ask why the administration is not applying the in-law requirement that those seeking citizenship cannot be welfare-reliant -- DHS/DOS guidelines exempt usage of most of the nearly 80 federal welfare programs from this standard.

90.title: On Fox, Sessions Discusses Senate Majority's Failure To Produce Budget
90.description: WASHINGTON, July 30—Uma Pemmaraju interviewed Sen. Sessions this weekend to discuss the looming government shutdown and the draconian defense cuts that will take place in coming months if the Senate does not take action. Sessions also spoke about the relentless efforts by the U.S. Department of Agriculture to increase the number of people on food stamps.

91.title: Lee On Gov't Funding Deadline: Senate Majority Hasn't Passed A Budget In 3 Years
91.description: WASHINGTON, July 30--On "America's News HQ" yesterday, Sen. Mike Lee (R-UT) noted that the last time the Senate's Democrat majority passed a budget, the iPad did not yet exist.

92.title: Flashback: Sessions Asks: Will President's Budget Chief Resign If Statements Shown To Be Wrong?
92.description:
In a recent campaign ad (http://youtu.be/FBorRZnqtMo), President Obama says that "I believe the only way to create an economy built to last is to strengthen the middle class. Asking the wealthy to pay a little more so we can pay down our debt in a balanced way." But neither his original budget nor his July 27 budget update would do so. In fact, the numbers in the President's budget submissions directly contradict claims he and his Administration have made.

In this video, from a February 2012 Budget Committee hearing, Jeffrey Zients, President Obama's budget director, is unable to even say if the President's budget would increase or decrease spending above the levels set in law from the August 2011 debt limit agreement.

93.title: 'Special Report' On USDA-Mexico SNAP Partnership
93.description: WASHINGTON, July 24—On "Special Report" recently, Bret Baier reported on the Obama Administration's aggressive efforts to expand enrollment in the food stamp program, including an outreach partnership between USDA and the Mexican government. To view Sessions' letter requesting more information on this recently discovered partnership, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/LLHHVK

94.title: FOX Discusses Budget Committee Finding On Disability Benefits, New Jobs
94.description: WASHINGTON, July 18--On "Happening Now" today, Fox News' Jon Scott and the Washington Times' Charlie Hurt discussed a new Budget Committee analysis showing that over the last three months, the number of Americans who began receiving Social Security Disability benefits outnumbered those who found new jobs. Additionally, the Congressional Budget Office recently prepared a report at Sen. Sessions' request about the growth in the program in recent years. To view that report, please click here (http://cbo.gov/publication/43432), and to view Sessions' statement about it, please click here (http://1.usa.gov/NzhScW).

95.title: 'Senator Reid, What's Your Plan?'
95.description: WASHINGTON, July 17--Sen. Sessions challenged Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid today on the Senate Democrats' three-year refusal to allow any budget to be worked on. Sessions asked an all-important question for the future of America that Majority Leader Reid has never answered: "They refuse even to write a budget and bring it to the floor for consideration. They have no financial plan for the future of America. *Senator Reid, what's your plan?*"

96.title: Sessions: 9th Circuit Refusing To Turn Over Contracts For Maui Conference
96.description:
WASHINGTON, July 17—Greta Van Susteren interviewed Sen. Sessions last night after he and Senator Grassley sent a letter to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals urging the Court to release contracts with details of their yearly conferences and to cancel their upcoming taxpayer-funded, million-dollar trip to Maui, Hawaii. Although the 2012 conference is currently moving forward as planned, the Court has canceled their scheduled 2013 conference in Monterey in the face of increased public scrutiny.

To view the Senators' letter, click here: http://budget.senate.gov/republican/public/index.cfm/files/serve/?File_id=4002fad2-1a97-44d7-b303-ca119d8ce99b

97.title: Sessions To Reid: DISCLOSE Your Plan For Spending Taxpayer Money
97.description: WASHINGTON, July 17--As the Senate was set to vote for a second time on the DISCLOSE Act, bill that did not even have sufficient support to move forward in that chamber, Sen. Sessions asked why the Senate's majority leadership has refused to disclose its financial vision for the nation. As of today, it has been 1,175 days since the Democrat-led Senate has passed a budget resolution.

98.title: Sessions To Push Vote On Senate Dems' Stealth $14 Billion Spending Increase
98.description:
WASHINGTON, July 17--Sen. Sessions delivered remarks on the Senate floor today about the controversial decision of the Senate majority leadership to file outlay levels that exceed, by $14 billion, the allowable limits from last August's debt limit agreement. Sessions announced that he would attempt to find an opportunity to raise a point of order, allowing each Senator to cast a vote on whether or not to break the spending limits.

To view background information about this issue, including both a brief and a detailed description, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/MFpdqt

99.title: Krauthammer Addresses Quadrupling Food Stamp Budget, Growth in Welfare Dependency
99.description: WASHINGTON, July 11—Last night on the O'Reilly Factor, Charles Krauthammer discussed the enormous growth in food stamp spending -- quadrupling in cost since 2001 -- and the fact that the program is no longer only targeted to those in need but that the goal has shifted to registering the largest possible number of individuals.

100.title: CNN: USDA Pushes 'Food Stamp Parties' As Way To Increase Registration
100.description: CNN recently reported on the U.S. Department of Agriculture's efforts to increase participation in the food stamp program by airing ads and urging state administrators to hold "food stamp parties."

101.title: Perino On Food Stamp Spending, Sessions' Reform Efforts
101.description: WASHINGTON, June 29--Fox News' "The Five" recently aired a segment on food stamp spending, which makes up 80 percent of the current farm bill. As Dana Perino noted, food stamp spending is now projected to remain permanently elevated: "How do we [keep] people and the government from going down this path... how do we help them with a pro-growth policy to make sure that they aren't going to need it in the future, and that -- from a moral standpoint we have an obligation to help them. I think that is worthwhile and a discussion we should have."

102.title: Special Report: Food Stamp Spending To Remain Elevated 'Long After' Economy Should Improve
102.description: WASHINGTON, June 27--Fox News' "Special Report" recently aired a segment on food stamp spending, which makes up 80 percent of the current farm bill. As Chief National Correspondent Jim Angle noted, food stamp spending is now projected to remain permanently elevated, even after the time the economy should have recovered.

103.title: WSJ's Steve Moore On Sessions' Food Stamp Reform Efforts
103.description: Yesterday on the "Willis Report," the Wall Street Journal's Steve Moore discussed efforts to reform the food stamp program, which has quadrupled in size over the past decade. Sen. Sessions recently proposed some modest reforms to restore certain eligibility rules--which would have saved about $11 billion from a $770 billion food stamp budget over the next decade--but the Senate's Democrat majority voted those amendments down.

104.title: Sessions Discusses Effort To Prevent States From Voiding Food Stamp Eligibility Rules
104.description: WASHINGTON, June 5—Sen. Sessions appeared on "America's Newsroom" this morning to discuss spending in the food stamp program, which has doubled over the past five years and quadrupled over the past ten. Much of the growth comes from expanded eligibility rules, with 39 states now having *no* statutory asset test for the program.

105.title: Senate Majority Party Blocks Effort To Restore Food Stamp Eligibility Rules Already In Law
105.description: "Fox & Friends" did a segment this morning examining the Senate's recent votes on Sen. Sessions' food stamp reform amendments. To view more information about those efforts, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/LkbVm2

106.title: Ninth Circuit Stands By Million-Dollar Maui Getaway: 'Cost-Effective And Productive'
106.description:
Megyn Kelly and Trace Gallagher reported today on the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals' response to Sens. Sessions and Grassley about the Court's planned Hawaii retreat, which is set to cost the taxpayers $1 million or more.

To view a joint statement from Sessions and Grassley after they received the Ninth Circuit's letter, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/MDFi27. To view their original letter asking for information about the retreat, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/KFvg1n.

107.title: Greta Interviews Sessions, Grassley As 9th Circuit Defends Fourth Hawaiian Getaway In Nine Years
107.description:
WASHINGTON, June 19--Greta Van Susteren interviewed Sen. Sessions and Sen. Grassley last night after the Senators received a response from the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals about a planned million-dollar judicial conference scheduled to be held in Maui, Hawaii. Sens. Sessions and Grassley had asked the Circuit if such a lavish retreat was necessary at a time of fiscal crisis, but the response from Ninth Circuit Chief Judge Alex Kozinski essential defended the event as "a way to provide for 'personal interaction' and a 'constructive and civil open exchange of ideas,'" according to the Hill newspaper.

Among the recreational activities currently planned for the conference: snorkeling, a floral design workshop, stand-up paddle board lessons, and something called "the Aloha Experience."

108.title: Sessions: Will One Senator Defend President's Claim That His Plan 'Pays Down Our Debt'?
108.description:
WASHINGTON, June 14--Sen. Sessions, Ranking Member of the Budget Committee, spoke on the floor to address the claim from President Obama that his budget proposal would "pay down our long-term debt."  In May, President Obama said he was "running to pay down the debt."  An aide also said, advancing the speech, that the President's plan "pays down our debt in a way that's balanced."  In reality, the President's budget produces $11 trillion in gross federal debt and increases spending by $1.5 trillion.  
Click here for more info: http://youtu.be/IF2TkI7R9n4

109.title: Sessions: Placing Maximum Number Of People On Food Stamps Is Wrong Policy Goal
109.description:
WASHINGTON, June 13--During the debate on the farm bill on the Senate floor today, Sen. Sessions spoke about his efforts to reform the food stamp program, spending for which makes up 80 percent of the farm bill.

Sessions addressed the rapid growth of the program over the past decade--participation has nearly tripled since 2001 and spending has doubled since 2008--and noted that the program has expanded even when the economy performed relatively well.

Over the next 10 years, food stamp spending is projected to be $770 billion, after a $4 billion cut proposed as part of the current bill. Yet some Senators have opposed efforts to reduce any spending on the program, prompting Sessions to ask, "[quote about is it our national goal to enroll as many people as possible?]"

To view additional information about Sessions' proposal to modestly reform food stamp and welfare in this country, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/KuC3MS

110.title: Sessions: Food Stamp And Welfare Reform Will Help More Americans Achieve Financial Independence
110.description:
WASHINGTON, June 8--Speaking on the Senate floor yesterday afternoon, Sen. Sessions unveiled a package of amendments to reform food stamps, a benefit program that expanded dramatically in recent years. Since 2001, food stamp rolls have nearly tripled, while spending on the program more than doubled since 2008. Indeed, food stamps are now the second-largest of nearly 80 federal welfare programs, including 17 nutrition support programs.

To view text of Sessions' remarks, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/LGbGPP

111.title: Sessions: CBO's New Long-Term Budget Outlook 'A Call To Action'
111.description:
WASHINGTON, June 7--Last night on the Senate floor, Sen. Sessions discussed CBO's new "Long-Term Budget Outlook," a yearly report that analyzes the financial future of the United States beyond the traditional 10-year budget window. The result, Sessions said, is "not a document that should give us comfort, but should be a call to action, really, as to what we need to do about the financial future of our country."

Among CBO's findings (all figures adjusted for inflation to 2012 levels):
• Over the next 20 years, high debt levels will lower the U.S.' cumulative economic output by roughly $21 trillion.

• By 2037, the federal government will spend $2.7 trillion per year in interest payments alone, representing more than a quarter of our entire budget that year and greater than the total federal budget in 2003.

• Each family's share of the federal debt will climb to $382,000 over the next 25 years, an additional $287,000 compared with today's levels.

• By 2025, mandatory health care spending, Social Security, and interest costs will consume 100 percent of revenues.

• CBO also warned that "growing debt... would increase the probability of a sudden fiscal crisis, during which investors would lose confidence in the government's ability to manage its budget and the government would thereby lose its ability to borrow at affordable rates."

112.title: Sessions: One Week Until Deadline For Admin To Provide Requested Info On Corporate Energy Loans
112.description:
WASHINGTON, June 5—Sen. Sessions appeared on "America's Newsroom" this morning to discuss the oversight effort he and House Oversight Chairman Darrell Issa have been pursuing with respect to preferential treatment that may have been given to certain energy corporations with connections to the Obama Administration. Sessions and Issa sent a letter last week, and Sessions said today that the Department of the Interior (DOI), to whom the letter was sent, has one more week to provide the requested info before Congress considers whether to use subpoenas to get it.

Sessions noted that he has been asking for the information in question for more than six months, yet to date the Administration has only provided a cursory reply with information already available on DOI's public website.

One of the companies in the Sessions-Issa inquiry, First Solar, received more than $3 billion in loan guarantees before recently laying off around 30 percent of its workforce. The company has also seen a "collapse" in its stock prices.

113.title: FOX Interviews Issa About Sessions-Issa Oversight Of Corporate Favoritism In Admin's Energy Loans
113.description: WASHINGTON, June 4—On "America's Newsroom" Friday, House Oversight Chairman Darrell Issa discussed the letter he and Sen. Jeff Sessions sent to the Department of Interior Secretary Ken Salazar about the Department's role in the Obama Administration's green energy initiatives. Sessions and Issa's oversight effort stems from two previous requests for information that Sessions sent about preferential treatment that was given to certain energy corporations that have close political ties to the Obama Administration. To view more information about the lawmakers' efforts, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/Kqu6pX

114.title: Fox: Sessions, Issa Pressing Admin For Stonewalled Info On Green Energy Loans
114.description: WASHINGTON, May 30--On last night's "Special Report," Bret Baier reported on the joint letter from Ranking Member Sessions and House Oversight Chairman Darrell Issa to Department of Interior Secretary Ken Salazar. In their letter, the lawmakers ask for information about certain fast-tracked energy corporations that may have received preferential treatment to operate on federal lands. To view the Sessions-Issa letter, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/LFQRTe

115.title: Sessions: Spending Scandals Reveal Government In 'Financial Chaos'
115.description:
WASHINGTON, May 22--Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today to reveal a stunning finding: although the Budget Control Act says that the Chairman of the Budget Committee must set discretionary outlays at the CBO's March baseline level, Chairman Kent Conrad instead used numbers derived from President Obama's budget, resulting in spending that will be $14 billion higher in FY 2013 than the law allows.

He also drew parallels between this finding and other recent scandals, including the GSA conference at Las Vegas, the Ninth Circuit judicial conference in Maui, and the Treasury Inspector General report that revealed more than $4 billion per year in child tax credits being sent to illegal immigrants who claim dependents that don't even live in the United States.

116.title: Shock: Senate Majority Files Senate FY13 Spending At Obama Budget Level, Not Budget Control Act
116.description: WASHINGTON, May 22--Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today to reveal a stunning finding: although the Budget Control Act says that the Chairman of the Budget Committee must set discretionary outlays at the CBO's March baseline level, Chairman Kent Conrad instead used numbers derived from President Obama's budget, resulting in spending that will be $14 billion higher in FY 2013 than the law allows.

117.title: Sessions Says Judicial Appropriations Must Be Examined In Light Of Conference Controversy
117.description: WASHINGTON, May 22—Appearing On "Fox & Friends" this morning, Sen. Sessions addressed the recent controversy surrounding the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals' judicial conference, scheduled for this August in Maui, Hawaii. Sessions drew parallels between this controversy and the scandal relating to the GSA's recent junket in Las Vegas, noting that President Obama has yet to assert the kind of managerial discipline to let government employees know that such expenditures are not acceptable during this time of fiscal crisis. Sessions also said that future judicial appropriations will have to be examined in light of this lavish conference.

118.title: WH Surrogate Repeats False, Discredited Claims About President's Budget
118.description:
WASHINGTON, May 21--On "Fox News Sunday" yesterday, University of Chicago economist and former Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers made repeated false claims about President Obama's FY 2013 budget, namely that it achieves $4 trillion in deficit reduction through a 3:1 ratio of spending cuts to tax increases.

In reality, the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office analyzed the President's plan and found just $519 billion in deficit reduction. In the absence of the President's budget, CBO projected that deficits from 2012 to 2022 would be $8.2 trillion. CBO's estimate after President Obama's budget found $7.6 trillion in deficits. The President's budget plan is able to achieve this amount of deficit reduction because his $1.5 trillion in spending *increases* are outweighed by an even greater amount ($2 trillion) of tax increases.

In fact, President Obama's own budget chief was unable this year to even describe what happens to spending under the President's plan; if he had answered the question, he would have been forced to admit that spending increases under the President's budget. To view that exchange, please click here: http://youtu.be/IF2TkI7R9n4

119.title: 'Stop it Now': Sessions Says Government Waste Can't Continue
119.description: WASHINGTON, May 17—Speaking yesterday on the Senate floor, Sen. Sessions said that as the nation's chief executive, President Obama has a responsibility to put an end to waste and abuse of taxpayer funds as soon as it's identified. Sessions noted that a recent Treasury Department IG report revealed that illegal immigrants have been receiving as much as $4 billion in tax credits every year by claiming dependents who don't even live in this country.

120.title: 'Stop it Today': Sessions Says Government Waste Can't Continue
120.description: WASHINGTON, May 17—Speaking yesterday on the Senate floor, Sen. Sessions said that as the nation's chief executive, President Obama has a responsibility to put an end to waste and abuse of taxpayer funds as soon as it's identified. Sessions noted that a recent Treasury Department IG report revealed that illegal immigrants have been receiving as much as $4 billion in tax credits every year by claiming dependents who don't even live in this country.

121.title: 0-99: Senate Unanimously Rejects President's Budget
121.description: For the second year in a row, President Obama's budget was rejected without a single vote in its favor in the United States Senate. This year's vote tally was slightly worse than last year's vote of 0-97.

122.title: Sessions Details Danger Of Majority's Budget Law Defiance As Debt Mounts
122.description: WASHINGTON, May 16--Speaking on the Senate floor today, Sen. Sessions detailed the dangers of the United States' current financial state. For example, total U.S. government debt exceeds that of the Eurozone and UK combined (http://1.usa.gov/IBkTc8), and the U.S.' per person government debt is worse than that of Greece (http://1.usa.gov/KxmEIT).

123.title: Sen. Wicker: Senate Majority Dodging Budget Law For Third Year
123.description: WASHINGTON, May 16—Sen. Roger Wicker spoke on the Senate floor today about the Democrat Senate's deliberate decision to ignore the law by not producing or passing a budget in more than three years.

124.title: 'Greetings From Washington, Send More Money'
124.description:
WASHINGTON, May 16--Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today during the debate on a number of different budget plans offered by Republicans, including three from Republican Senators and one approved by the House of Representatives. Because no member of the majority party has been willing to call up President Obama's plan, Republicans introduced his budget as well. Last year, President Obama's budget was defeated in the Senate by a vote of 0-97.

Sen. Sessions characterized his Democrat colleagues' refusal to budget as: "We're in Washington, we're having fun... send more money."

125.title: Ahead Of Budget Votes, GOP Senators Address Senate Majority's Unwillingness To Offer Plan
125.description: WASHINGTON, May 15—Sens. Mike Johanns, Jon Kyl, Johnny Isakson, Tom Coburn and Dean Heller joined in a colloquy on the Senate floor today to discuss the Senate majority's failure to confront the unsustainable debt course our country is currently on.

126.title: 1,111 Days Ago: Last Time Senate Majority Brought A Budget To The Floor
126.description: WASHINGTON, May 14—In a colloquy on the Senate floor today, Sens. Ron Johnson, John Barrasso, Kay Bailey Hutchison, and Bob Corker discussed the failure of the Senate's Democrat majority to produce or pass a budget in 1,111 days. Since that time, Congress has spent $10.4 trillion and added $4.5 trillion to the national debt.

127.title: 'Extreme Financial Malpractice': Steve Moore On 3rd Anniversary Of Senate Dems' Refusal To Budget
127.description: WASHINGTON, April 30--This morning on "America's Newsroom," Steve Moore and Bill Hemmer discussed yesterday's milestone: it has now officially been three years since the Senate's Democrat majority has adopted a budget plan.

128.title: On Fox, Sessions Marks Third Anniversary Of Dem Senate's No Budget Spectacle
128.description: WASHINGTON, April 27--Sunday, April 29th will mark the third-year anniversary of the last time the Senate's Democrat majority passed a budget resolution.

129.title: Sessions Invites Majority To Explain Their Refusal To Adopt A Budget
129.description: WASHINGTON, April 26--Speaking on the Senate floor today , Sen. Sessions challenged his colleagues to come to the floor and defend the Democrat-led Senate's failure to produce a budget plan (Sunday the 29th will mark exactly three years since the Senate last adopted a budget).

130.title: THREE YEARS
130.description: WASHINGTON, April 26--Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today to mark the 3-year anniversary since the last time Senate Democrats passed a budget resolution. The Washington Post recently noted that this milestone, which occurs this Sunday, April 29, is "a record since Congress adopted budget process reforms in 1974."

131.title: Senators Urge Colleagues To Find A Way To Pay For Postal Bill, Uphold Agreed-To Spending Levels
131.description: WASHINGTON, April 25—Yesterday, Sen. Sessions raised a budget point of order against the postal bill currently before the Senate because it would increase the deficit by $34 billion, thereby breaking the debt limit deal agreed to last summer. (Under that agreement, every dollar of debt limit increase was tied to a dollar of spending cuts.) Several Senators joined Sessions on the floor in support of keeping the debt limit deal and finding spending cuts to offset the cost of the postal bill. However, the vote to waive the point of order was agreed upon, thereby allowing spending and debt above the limits set in law.

132.title: Wasserman Schultz Claims House GOP Blocked Obama Budget Proposal That She Voted Against
132.description:
WASHINGTON, April 25—Ahead of April 29, the three-year anniversary since Senate Democrats last passed a budget, DNC Chairwoman Debbie Wasserman Schultz was asked last night about her attempts to draw a contrast between Republican and Democrat budget visions.

Wasserman Schultz was asked about a previous interview in which she said that "the Senate should take up a budget, and I expect that they will... I'm confident the Senate will take up a budget." Those comments drew attention since Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid had previously made clear that the Senate would not take a budget this year, as it did not in the two prior. Since that previous interview, Senate Democrats cancelled at the last-minute what would have been their first budget mark-up in more than two years. In her interview last night, the Democrat Party chair declined to say again that the Senate should pass its own budget plan, effectively retreating from her previous view.

Instead, the DNC Chair accused House Republicans of blocking the President's plan, even though she (along with Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi and Minority Whip Steny Hoyer) was among those who voted against it (it fell 414-0 in the House). Notably, in addition to declining to bring up their own financial plan, the Senate's Majority has also declined to bring up President Obama's.

To view Wasserman Schultz's previous interview on this topic, please 
 click here: http://youtu.be/drvq2BqDt0I.

133.title: Ahead Of Key Budget Vote, Sessions Urges Senate Not To Break Debt Deal With Extra Borrowing
133.description:
WASHINGTON, April 24--Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today ahead of a key procedural vote on the postal reform bill.

Although Sessions acknowledged the underlying bill might have merit, he pointed out that it violates the spending agreement from the Budget Control Act (the debt limit deal) agreed to just last August. In that bill, spending was cut by $2.1 trillion as a condition for raising the debt ceiling.

Sessions said: "We need not to kill reform of the postal service; we need to send this bill back to committee, let them produce legislation that either spends not so much... or if they do spend money, pay for the money with cuts in spending that are perfectly available... We've got GSA off in Las Vegas in hot tubs on taxpayers' money. We could pay for this bill if it's so important that we have to do it."

134.title: Sessions Announces Decisive Procedural Vote Today On Postal Bill
134.description: WASHINGTON, April 23--Sen. Sessions announced on the Senate floor today that he would raise a budget point of order against the postal bill currently pending before the Senate. In order for the Senate to consider the bill, 60 Senators would have to vote to waive the point of order, thus agreeing to spend more money than the Budget Control Act levels set forth in law.

135.title: Full Remarks: Sessions On Senate Dems' Cancellation Of Legally-Required Budget Markup
135.description: Having decided not to produce a budget in committee last year, and having failed to adopt a budget for the last two years, Senate Dems canceled this year's overdue Budget Committee markup of a plan, effectively ensuring that 2012 will be the third consecutive year the chamber's majority declines to offer a budget plan.

136.title: Republicans Protest Cancellation Of Budget Markup As Dem Senate Goes Third Year Without A Budget
136.description:
WASHINGTON, April 20—After not adopting a budget resolution since April 29, 2009—1,087 days ago—the Senate's Democrat majority appeared set this week to at least hold a mark-up in the Budget Committee; that is, debate and amend the measure before voting whether or not to send it to the full Senate. At the last minute, however, the Senate's Democrat leadership and Budget Committee Chairman Kent Conrad cancelled the mark-up. Senators were instead only permitted to offer opening statements; no amendments were considered and no votes were cast.

Every Republican Senator attended the committee meeting to urge the chamber's Democrat Majority leadership to abandon its resistance to taking up a budget plan.

137.title: 'Meetings, Discussions, Frameworks' No Substitute For Accountability Of Public Budget Votes
137.description:
WASHINGTON, April 18—The Senate Budget Committee was, after months of delay, scheduled to hold an official mark-up today in which amendments would be considered and a final vote would be held. But that mark-up was cancelled, and instead Senators were only permitted to give opening statements before the committee meeting was ended.

During his statement, Ranking Member Sessions criticized the mark-up's cancellation, saying that "We've had secret meetings, committees, discussions, outlines, and frameworks, but when it's laid out in real numbers... people can then look at it and express their view. They either like it or don't like it, but it has reality to it, and the kind of power to it, that just talk does not have...

There has been... a systematic plan for several years on behalf of Sen. Reid, I guess, and the Democratic leadership, to avoid votes on budgets. To avoid being accountable for having a real plan for the future... So I have to say, I'm disappointed that we're not being able to have the kind of markup that ought to be basic to the statutory duty of this committee to fulfill its responsibility to produce a budget."

138.title: Sessions: How Can Dems Call For Higher Taxes When They Won't Write A Budget?
138.description:
WASHINGTON, April 19—In remarks on the Senate floor today today, Sen. Sessions addressed the Democrat-led Senate's failure to put forward a budget for the past three years. Sessions argued that no elected official should call for higher taxes until they're willing to stand behind a budget plan that lays out taxing and spending priorities for working Americans' tax dollars.

Sessions pointed to the exact section in the U.S. Code book that requires Congress to pass a budget.

139.title: On Greta, Sessions Addresses Last-Minute Cancellation Of Budget Markup
139.description:
WASHINGTON, April 19--Last night, Sen. Sessions appeared on "On the Record w/ Greta Van Susteren" to discuss the Democrat Senate leadership's last-minute cancellation of a budget mark-up yesterday.

Sen. Sessions stated: "I truly believe the president decided, not long after the Simpson-Bowles commission met, that he was not going to make tough decisions on tough spending issues. Harry Reid decided the same thing. For three years—through a systemic, deliberate, planned effort—they have violated the statutory requirement to bring up a budget, avoided having multiple votes that when you move a budget forward you are entitled to have—50 hours of debate and amendments—and it is kind of a sad thing, frankly."

140.title: Chuck Todd Discusses Senate Budget Process
140.description: WASHINGTON, April 19--MSNBC's Chuck Todd interviewed Senate Budget Committee Chairman Kent Conrad today about why the Senate's Majority has declined to produce a budget resolution since 2009.

141.title: Sessions on Senate Dem Majority's 'Deliberate And Determined' Effort To Avoid  Budget Votes
141.description:
WASHINGTON, April 18—Sen. Sessions delivered closing remarks today at what he called a "faux mark-up"—a Budget Committee meeting at which Senators were not allowed to offer amendments or hold any votes on any aspect of a budget plan.

Sessions stated: "The fact is it's now three years—three years—into the execution of a deliberate and determined policy by the Democratic leadership of the United States Senate to avoid responsibility for the financial future of America. It's not acceptable for the Senate leadership to not face up to the challenge of our time."

Sessions went on, asking rhetorically: "Is it really okay to wait until after the election to vote? Is that what the American expect of us? Are they satisfied that we say, 'Oh, we can't take votes close to an election. That might be tough. We don't want to do that'? I don't think so."

143.title: Sessions Comments On Dem. Leadership's Blockade Of Budget Mark-Up

145.title: Cavuto: Budget Committee Chart Reveals That US Debt Trumps EU And UK Combined
145.description: WASHINGTON, April 11—Today on "Your World," Neil Cavuto reported on a new chart from the Senate Budget Committee minority staff showing that the U.S. is carrying more debt than the Eurozone and UK combined—$15.1 trillion vs. $12.7 trillion. The Euro Zone also has a larger population (332 million to the U.S.' 313 million), meaning that both per person and as a share of the economy, the U.S. is carrying more total debt.

146.title: Senate Dems: Maybe We'll Do A Budget—After The Election
146.description: WASHINGTON, April 9—Appearing On Fox News Sunday yesterday, Senate Budget Committee Chairman Kent Conrad said that although he plans to hold a budget mark-up in committee, the party's leadership had "probably quite correctly" decided that the American public would not get to see how their representatives voted on a budget until after the election.

147.title: Fox Report On Senate Dem Majority's Desire To Avoid Budget Votes
147.description: WASHINGTON, April 9--FOX News' "Happening Now" did a report today on a recent ruling from the Senate Parliamentarian that said that Democrat Senate leaders cannot block budget votes this year, as they had sought to do.

148.title: Stumped Again: WH Has No Answer For Why Senate Dems Won't Write A Budget
148.description: WASHINGTON, April 4—White House Press Secretary Jay Carney struggled last night to justify the Senate's ongoing refusal to present and adopt a budget plan in the chamber, despite the legal requirement to do so. The Senate's Democrat majority has not offered a budget in more than 1,000 days, even though, as host Bret Baier notes, budgets only require a simple majority to pass the chamber: "It's not 60 votes. It's all Democrats. All Democrats could vote on a budget, they could vote on it tomorrow and they could pass it if they put it on the table. You know that. So why doesn't the president call Harry Reid and say 'do that'?"

149.title: Head Of Democratic Party Directly Contradicts Reid On Need For Senate Budget
149.description:
WASHINGTON, April 4—Last night on "On the Record," DNC Chairwoman Debbie Wasserman Schultz contradicted earlier statements by Majority Leader Harry Reid that the Senate's Democrat majority did not need to write and adopt a budget plan this year (after not having done so for over 1,000 days).

Last year, Sen. Reid said "it would be foolish" for Senate Democrats to write a budget (http://lat.ms/HkQNtM). In February, he went further, saying that "we do not need to bring a budget to the floor this year" (http://bit.ly/ySSSNI). He even expanded his pronouncement to include the yet-unseen plan from his Budget Committee Chairman: "Now, Sen. Conrad may mark something up in his Budget Committee... It doesn't have to come to the floor" (http://bit.ly/Ho1kjO).

But last night, Rep. Wasserman Schultz said that "I'd ask that you stipulate that the Senate should take up a budget, and I expect that they will... I'm confident the Senate will take up a budget... don't put words in Senator Reid's mouth and say that because a budget hasn't come to the floor yet that it won't."

[Note: The legal deadline to report a budget out of committee was April 1st.]

150.title: O'Reilly Discusses Axelrod's Response To Senate Dems' Budget Law Defiance
150.description: WASHINGTON, April 3—Last week, Bill O'Reilly discusssed the inabability of David Axelrod, a senior campaign Obama advisor, to explain why the Senate's Democrat majority has refused to offer a budget resolution for well over 1,000 days.

151.title: Lou Dobbs On $17 Trillion Long-Term Funding Gap In President's Health Law
151.description:
WASHINGTON, April 2—Last week, Lou Dobbs examined a new Budget Committee minority staff analysis of the long-term costs associated with President Obama's health care law. The new projections, based on the Administration's own numbers, show a long-term funding shortfall of at least $17 trillion. If the Administration's estimates turn out to be overly optimistic, the shortfall could be much larger.

Taken together with the unfunded liabilities for other federal health programs—that is, promises made but for which no money is set aside—the government's 75-year unfunded obligations reach a staggering $82 trillion.

152.title: Stunning Finding: President's Health Law Creates $17 Trillion In Unfunded Financial Obligations
152.description:
WASHINGTON, March 29--On the Senate floor today, Ranking Member Sessions announced that a new Budget Committee analysis has found that the long-term, unfunded liabilities associated with President Obama's health care law will reach $17 trillion. The Committee's analysis is based on the Obama Administration's own numbers as well as those from the Congressional Budget Office. It is a modest, conservative estimate and yet is still more than double that of Social Security.

At a "bipartisan fiscal responsibility summit" in 2009, President Obama's then-OMB Director, Peter Orszag, stated: "To my fellow budget hawks in this room and in the rest of the country, let me be very clear: Health care reform is entitlement reform. The path to fiscal responsibility must run directly through health care." But despite this emphatic statement, the nation's unfunded liabilities--money we must spend but for which there is no source of funds set aside--increased from $65 trillion to $82 trillion since the health law was passed.

To view a graph depicting the increase in unfunded obligations brought on by the law, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/H4Lk66.

153.title: Thune On Greta: Democrat Senate Will Punt Again On Budget
153.description: WASHINGTON, March 23—On Wednesday, U.S. Senator John Thune (R-S.D.), Chairman of the Senate Republican Conference, joined FOX News' "On the Record w/ Greta Van Susuteren" to discuss Rep. Paul Ryan's FY13 budget proposal.

154.title: Top Dem Wrong On Health Law Spending
154.description:
WASHINGTON, March 22--In an interview on FOX News today, a top Democrat official, Congresswoman Debbie Wasserman-Shultz (D-FL) addressed the rising costs associated with President Obama's health care law by claiming that the price tag had not doubled from the $900 billion in ten-year spending the president originally promised. However, a recently released report from the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office put the cost of just the coverage expansion at $1.76 trillion between now and 2022. Importantly, this price tag does not include other costs associated with the law, such as implementation or closing the Medicare "donut hole." However, a true ten-year window begins in 2014, the first year that the major spending provisions go into effect (the spending was delayed by four years to gimmick the original score). Thus, over a true 10-year window when all spending is taken into account, Senate Budget Committee minority staff calculations (using CBO's estimates) show that the cost of the president's health law totals at least $2.6 trillion, nearly three times what the president promised.
 
Additionally, Congresswoman Wasserman-Shultz, who is also the head of the Democratic National Committee, characterized the CBO report's findings on the coverage impact of the health law: "You're not going to have people lose insurance... You're not quoting the report accurately."  But CBO estimates that anywhere from 4 million to 20 million people will lose their employer-provided health insurance as a result of the law.  Some estimate that figure to be dramatically higher.

155.title: Sessions Responds To Attacks On Ryan, House GOP From Budgetless Senate Majority
155.description:
WASHINGTON, March 21—Speaking on the Senate floor yesterday, Sen. Sessions addressed attacks on House Republicans from Majority Leader Harry Reid, Budget Chairman Kent Conrad, and Sen. Patty Murray. The senior Democrat Senators argued that the Senate's Democrat Majority had no obligation to produce a budget and that the recent debt-limit deal passed by Congress (the Budget Control Act, or BCA) somehow represented the maximum amount of money Congress is allowed to save. These comments from leading Democrats in Washington have a special irony given that they want to repeal half of the spending cuts in the BCA—in fact, the president's budget does precisely that (increasing spending $1.6 trillion in total above current projections).

The BCA calls for $2.1 trillion (half from discretionary) in net spending cuts over ten years from a previously estimated spending level of about $47 trillion (meaning spending would still increase by about 60% and debt would grow by about 75%). In their FY 2013 budget plan, House Republicans trimmed an additional $5.3 trillion in spending relative to the president's budget request over ten years (and reduced discretionary spending by $19 billion for next year relative to current law). Murray and other Democrat leaders asserted that this was "outrageous." To put the $2.1 trillion net figure in perspective, the president's health law alone will spend $2.6 trillion during its first full ten years of implementation (fiscal years 2014-2023).

156.title: Stumped: Axelrod Can't Explain Why Senate Dems Won't Pass A Budget
156.description:
WASHINGTON, March 21--On FOX News last night, senior Obama advisor David Axelrod was unable to explain why the Senate's Democrat majority has refused to produce a budget resolution for well over 1,000 days. He initially tried to suggest that "dynamics in the Senate" were to blame, but as anchor Bret Baier pointed out, budgets are privileged documents that only require a simple majority to pass.

To view a timeline of budget battles during this Congress, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/o0pgPk  

To view Sessions' comments on what would happen if GOP were to gain Senate majority: http://youtu.be/S7y1v-EYz4E

157.title: Sessions: If Republicans Get Senate Majority, We Will Pass A Budget
157.description:
WASHINGTON, March 20--Sen. Sessions, Ranking Member of the Senate Budget Committee, jointed with Chairman Paul Ryan and members of the House Budget Comittee as they unveiled their FY13 budget plan to address America's growing financial crisis.  By contrast, the Democrat-run Senate has failed to deliver a budget plan for 1,056 days.  This is the third year running that they will forego this fundamental obligation, even as America's debt continues its dangerous ascent.  In his remarks, Sessions addressed how things would be different were Republicans to have the privelege of a senate majority:

"We have never needed a budget more now than we need it today: we are facing a systemic threat to America's financial health... Senate Democrats have abandoned their obligations, and have refused to offer a budget for now three straight years now...If the voters give the Republicans in the Senate the honor of having the majority [next year], we will work with the House to pass a congressional budget. It will be an honest budget. It will change the debt course of America."

158.title: Senators Address Soaring Cost Of President's Health Law
158.description:
WASHINGTON, March 20—In a colloquy on the Senate floor yesterday, Sen. Sessions joined with Sens. Ron Johnson, Jon Kyl, John Boozman, and Pat Roberts to address the rapidly increasing cost projections for President Obama's health care law.

In a January 2009 address to a joint session of Congress, the president declared that "when you add it all up, the plan that i'm proposing will cost around 900 billion over 10 years," but the true 10-year cost of the law, when fully implemented, is now estimated to be at least $2.6 trillion.

159.title: Sessions: Americans Have A Right to Be Angry Over Health Law's Surging Costs
159.description: WASHINGTON, March 19--Speaking on the Senate floor today, Sen. Sessions addressed the soaring cost projections for President Obama's health care law, which have now reached nearly triple what he originally promised the American people. Sessions stated: "This is the kind of thing that [has] the American people are asking us, 'Are you crazy? How can you borrow 40 cents of every dollar you spend? ... What's the matter with you people?'"

160.title: Dem Leaders Run From Budget Deadline As Health Law Threatens Nation's Finances
160.description:
WASHINGTON, March 18--Appearing on FOX News' "America's News HQ" today, Sen. Sessions discussed the nearing legal deadline for Senate Democrats to produce a budget (the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 requires the Senate Budget Committee to complete action on a resolution by April 1, and requires passage by the full Senate by April 15). Despite this unambiguous statutory requirement, the Budget Committee has taken no action to even begin work on a budget. In fact, it has now been 1,054 days--nearly three years--since Senate Democrats have produced a budget at all.

This stands in sharp contrast to the record of House Republicans, which passed a budget last year and which is set to introduce this year's budget next week.

Rather than confront the nation's debt threat, Senate Democrats have resorted to political tactics on unrelated matters, as well as attacks on the House Republican budget even in the absence of a plan of their own.

Sessions also addressed new cost projections for the president's health law, which the Congressional Budget Office last week found will cost nearly twice what the president originally promised, or nearly three times the promised amount once the law is fully implemented.

161.title: Sessions And Johnson Engage In Colloquy To Discuss Broken Promises Of President's Health Law
161.description: WASHINGTON, March 16--Earlier this week, Budget Committee Ranking Member Jeff Sessions and Budget Committee member Ron Johnson participated in a colloquy on the Senate floor to discuss the broken promises associated with the president's health care law--including that it would reduce the deficit, boost the economy, and improve Americans' quality of care.

162.title: Special Report Examines 'Substantial' Cost Increase For President's Health Law
162.description: WASHINGTON, March 15--Last night on Special Report with Bret Baier, correspondent Jim Angle examined a new Congressional Budget Office report that shows the cost of the president's health care law is now nearly double what he originally promised. As Sen. Sessions has noted, the true 10-year cost when the law is fully implemented will be even higher, at $2.6 trillion.

163.title: Reid Manufactures Phony Crisis To Conceal Dreadful Record Of Senate's Dem Majority
163.description: WASHINGTON, March 14--Defending the interests of workers in Alabama and across the country in a passionate address on the Senate floor today, Sen. Sessions took the Senate's Democrat leadership to task for failing to address the country's most pressing issues--producing a budget, developing more American energy, reducing costly and harmful regulations, and streamlining the tax code to allow American businesses to compete in the global marketplace.

164.title: Grassley: Dems Manufactured Judicial 'Vacancy Crisis' To Hide Budget Failure
164.description: WASHINGTON, March 13--Speaking on the Senate floor this evening, Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-IA) explained that Senate Democrat leaders, who have not offered a budget plan in over three years, are attempting to hide their failure by manufacturing a controversy over the rate of confirmation for judicial nominees.

165.title: Sessions Delivers Opening Statement At Hearing On FY13 Defense Budget
165.description: WASHINGTON, March 6—Sen. Sessions delivered an opening statement today at a Committee hearing on President Obama's 2013 Department of Defense budget request. Sessions stated: "We should accomplish the required cuts in our deficit with reductions to all spending, not primarily defense. Today, entitlement spending makes up sixty percent of our budget while defense makes up less than twenty percent. We should not allow the prospect of an additional $500 billion in cuts to national security spending to continue, while automatic entitlement spending continues relatively unscathed."

166.title: Honest Budget Act: Roby On FOX Business Calls For End To Gimmicks
166.description:
WASHINGTON, March 1--Appearing on FOX Business yesterday, U.S. Rep. Martha Roby discussed the Honest Budget Act, a legislative package to put an end to the most egregious budget gimmicks that Washington uses to conceal and enable hundreds of billions of dollars in deficit spending.

One of the Honest Budget Act's nine planks is a proposal to make President Obama's proposed federal "pay freeze" real: despite his promise in 2010 to freeze federal worker salaries, roughly 70 percent of federal workers have continued to receive annual or biannual raises of 2-3 percent. The Honest Budget Act would simply make the federal pay freeze real, saving roughly $1 billion annually.

Rep. Roby introduced the Honest Budget Act in the House of Representatives last month; her legislation is a companion to a bill introduced in the Senate last year by Budget Committee Ranking Member Jeff Sessions.

167.title: Sessions: President's Health Law 'A Hammer Blow' To Working Americans
167.description:
WASHINGTON, February 29—Sen. Sessions delivered an opening statement today at a Committee hearing to discuss the fiscal unsustainability of America's current healthcare policies.
