In his statement, Senator Sessions addressed a variety of pressing concerns, including the President's health care law, his budget proposal, and his refusal to acknowledge that we are on an unsustainable path. Sessions remarked: "Our national debt per person now equals nearly $45,000, more than Greece. The President's budget plan, sent to Congress, would grow our total debt by another $11 trillion.  By the end of ten years, interest payments will be $850 billion annually.
Similarly, the President's health care policies, rather than tackle the long-term drivers of our debt like Medicare, simply raided the program to pay for new entitlement spending and puts the entire budget on a dangerously unsustainable path.
In fact, today marks the fourth consecutive year the President has ignored the legal requirement -- the Medicare "trigger" -- to submit a legislative proposal to Congress that addresses Medicare's coming insolvency."

168.title: Sessions' Opening Remarks At Hearing With Defense Secretary
168.description: WASHINGTON, February 28--Sen. Sessions delivered an opening statement today at a Committee hearing with Defense Secretary Leon Panetta and Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Gen. Martin Dempsey to examine the president's FY 2013 defense budget request.

169.title: Panetta Agrees: Our Debt Path Threatens Our National Security
169.description: WASHINGTON, February 28--In a Budget Committee hearing today, Secretary of Defense Leon Panetta agreed with former Joint Chiefs Chairman Admiral Mike Mullen that the country's debt path represents a grave threat to our national security. He also called on Congress to undo the Budget Control Act sequester mechanism, which he and Sen. Sessions agreed would have a harmful effect on military readiness and capabilities. As Sen. Sessions noted, "We can't just balance this budget on the back of the Defense Department. And if we break faith with those fabulous men and women who have been deployed repeatedly--away from their families, placing their lives at risk--if they see what we've done as disproportionately targeting them for the wasteful Washington spending that's been going on, we would have broken faith with some of the best people this country has produced."

170.title: U.S. Per-Person Government Debt Worse Than Greece
170.description: WASHINGTON, February 24—On America Live, Megyn Kelly aired a segment on a chart released by Ranking Member Jeff Sessions (R-AL) and the Senate Budget Committee minority, revealing that, at $44,215 for every person in the United States, America's per capita government debt is worse than even Greece.  Click here to see the chart: http://1.usa.gov/ArnjEi

171.title: Geithner Refuses To Say Whether Obama Budget Cuts Spending
171.description:
WASHINGTON, February 16—Following up on earlier testimony from White House budget chief Jeffrey Zients, Sen. Sessions asked Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner if the president's budget proposes to increase or decrease spending relative to the levels that Congress and the president agreed to in August. Once again, the witness refused to give a direct answer. In reality, spending increases by $1.5 trillion over the levels set by the Budget Control Act.

To view Zients' testimony, please click here: http://youtu.be/IF2TkI7R9n4

172.title: Second Year In A Row: Geithner Says President's Budget Plan 'Unsustainable'
172.description:
WASHINGTON, February 16—Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner today admitted under questioning from Sen. Sessions that the president's own budget is "unsustainable." Sec. Geithner made a similar admission last year, when he said that "with the president's plan, even if Congress were to enact it and even if Congress were to hold it and reduce those deficits to three percent of GDP over the next five years, we would still be left with a very large interest burden and unsustainable obligations over time." To view last year's testimony, please click here: http://youtu.be/WdcQGJF_jmY.

To view a chart showing spending increases under the president's plan, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/yPP0by.

173.title: Sessions Delivers Opening Remarks At Geithner Hearing
173.description: WASHINGTON, February 16—Sen. Sessions delivered an opening statement today at a Committee hearing with Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner to examine President Obama's 2013 budget request. Sessions stated: "History will judge our conversation today. Do you believe that the president's budget provides the solution to our fiscal problems? Do you believe that $11.2 trillion in new federal debt, annual interest payments approaching $1 trillion a year, and a budget where health care spending grows twice as fast as our economy, is a sustainable future?"

174.title: America's Captain Absent From Deck, Sessions Warns
174.description: WASHINGTON, February 16— Speaking on the Senate Floor Tuesday, Sen. Sessions explained that the interest on America's debt is the fastest growing major item in the federal budget and poses a severe risk to America's fiscal health and economic security. Overall, under the president's budget plan our debt will increase another 11 trillion dollars over the next 10 years, reaching a total of 26 trillion dollars. Despite the widely acknowledge danger presented by the rapid and unsustainable accumulation of gross federal debt, President Obama continues to accelerate the country toward fiscal crisis. In describing the situation, Sessions offered an analogy: "The president, the man who is captain of the ship, is having lunch somewhere while the ship is heading to the shoals and not providing any leadership to get us off this path."

175.title: White House, Senate Dem Leaders Fear Open And Honest Budget Debate
175.description: WASHINGTON, February 15—On the Senate floor yesterday, Sen. Sessions expressed grave concern with Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid's announced decision not to put forward a budget for the third year in a row, as well as the misleading answers from Obama budget chief Jeff Zients at a committee hearing yesterday. Under direct questioning from Sessions, Zients refused to answer whether spending under the Obama budget would increase or decrease from the levels currently set in law. In fact, spending is set to increase over the levels agreed to in current law, for a total rate of increase of 62 percent over the next 10 years.

176.title: Sessions' Opening Statement At Hearing To Examine Transportation Budget
176.description: WASHINGTON, February 15--At a Budget Committee hearing today to examine President Obama's 2013 transportation budget, Sen. Sessions reminded the audience that although President Obama promised that his stimulus plan would devote significant investments to the nation's roads and bridges, only a fraction of the total bill actually went to that purpose.

177.title: Sessions' Opening Statement At Hearing With Obama's Budget Chief
177.description: WASHINGTON, February 14--Sen. Sessions delivered an opening statement today at a Committee hearing with OMB Acting Director Jeffrey Zients. Sessions pointed out that "Mr. Zeints must remember—he works for the American people, not the Obama campaign. And the American people have a right to know the truth."

178.title: White House Offers New Defense For Misleading Country On Budget Law
178.description: WASHINGTON, February 14—Note: At a Budget Committee's hearing today, Office of Management and Budget Acting Director Jeffrey Zients defended the claim from President Obama's chief of staff that Senate Democrats aren't bothering to offer a budget resolution this year saying they require 60 votes. By law, a budget resolution requires only 51 votes—yet Senate Democrats have not brought one to the floor for public examination, amendment, and debate for 1,020 days.  Zeints' claim, remarkably, was that Lew was referring to the previously passed Budget Control Act—the deal to raise the debt ceiling. A review of the video above, which includes both Zeints' comments today and Lew's original remarks, reveals the absurdity of this explanation.

In truth, the budget plan submitted by the president would increase spending by $1.5 trillion over the next 10 years relative to current projections. Over that time, the federal government will spend a total of $47 trillion, up from $45.5 trillion projected under the already enacted Budget Control Act—producing by the president's own projections an additional $11.2 trillion in gross debt.

NOTE: To view a detailed breakdown of proposed spending increases using numbers from President Obama's own budget, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/yRREwf.

To view the CNN segment (and additional background info in the video's description, please click here: http://youtu.be/aNxzQUyZu_U).

185.title: White House Misleads Country On Budget Law
185.description:
WASHINGTON, February 12—Under the law, a budget requires only 51 votes to pass the Senate—not 60. Jack Lew, the president's former director of the Office of Management and Budget (the top budget post in the administration) and current Chief of Staff, should be more familiar than most with this law. But today on CNN's "State of the Union," Lew falsely asserted that a budget requires 60 votes to pass. (Previously, another senior Democrat made the same claim: http://youtu.be/ifvp5P7U5AU.)

The controversy over Senate Democrats' failure to budget escalated recently when Majority Leader Reid declared that Senate Democrats "do not need to bring a budget to the floor this year." This would mark the third consecutive year—a record—that the Democrat Senate failed to offer a budget plan to the American people. Last year, they didn't even draft one for presentation in committee—keeping it a closely guarded secret, never shared with the public. As of today, it has been 1,019 days since the Senate's Democrat majority has offered a budget plan on the floor of the Senate.

Federal Reserve Chairman was asked about the uncertainty connected with the lack of a budget plan at a Budget Committee hearing this month and replied in part "...Is uncertainty negative on growth? I think it is."

Subsequently, ABC's Jake Tapper asked WH Spokesman Jay Carney about the situation at the daily press briefing. Here is an excerpt from that exchange:

TAPPER: "The White House has no opinion about whether or not the Senate should pass a budget? The president is going to introduce one, the Fed chair says not having one is bad for growth, but the White House has no opinion?"

CARNEY: "I have no opinion, the White House has no opinion..."

Ranking Member Sessions, describing the shirking of responsibility from the Senate's leaders said this: "By refusing to lay out a budget plan for public examination the Democrat Senate has forfeited the high privilege to lead this chamber."

186.title: Carney: White House Has 'No Opinion' On Senate Dems' Refusal To Work On Budget Plan
186.description:
WASHINGTON, February 8--In today's White House press briefing, Press Secretary Jay Carney struggled to justify Majority Leader Harry Reid's announced decision to keep a from coming to the floor of the Democrat-held Senate (for the third consecutive year - a record).

NOTE: To view Chairman Bernanke's comments (referenced in the clip) at a Budget Committee hearing yesterday, please click here: http://youtu.be/jqmq_S1YcbQ. President Obama's budget will be submitted on Monday, February 13. Ranking Member Sessions has said (http://1.usa.gov/yUUwpS) that Senator Reid's announcement that his Senate Democrat majority will not allow a budget resolution to move forward for the third consecutive year effectively means they have declared President Obama's budget "dead on arrival" and have "forfeited the high privilege to lead this chamber."

187.title: Sessions: Under Obama, Government Getting Bigger And Middle Class Getting Smaller
187.description:
WASHINGTON, February 7—Speaking today at the Senate Budget Committee with Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke, Sessions discussed the growth of government and diminishing paychecks for hardworking taxpayers: 
"The Congressional Budget Office's new outlook confirms that our deficit will top $1 trillion for the fourth straight year. And the deficits we face in the outyears, the next decade, are even more relentless and systemic. In just three years, we have accumulated almost $5 trillion in new gross debt -- during which time the total number of Americans working has decreased by 1.2 million. We have even fewer Americans working today than more than 11 years ago. Federal spending, in real dollars, has increased 53 percent in ten years, while real wages for the average American have declined 7 percent. The government is getting bigger and the middle class is getting smaller."

188.title: Bernanke Addresses Economic Impact Of Having No Senate Dem Budget Plan

189.title: Sessions' Opening Remarks At Bernanke Hearing
189.description: WASHINGTON, February 7--Sen. Sessions delivered an opening statement today at a Committee hearing with Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke. 190.title: CBO Director: Debt Poses Great Risk If Left Unaddressed
190.description: WASHINGTON, February 3--At a Budget Committee Hearing yesterday, Congressional Budget Office Director Doug Elmendorf agreed with Sen. 202.title: 1,002 Days Later: Sessions' Opening Remarks At First Senate Budget Hearing of 2012
