Sessions addressed the theme of President Obama's State of the Union address two days earlier (an 'America Built to Last'), explaining that one can't make a nation built to last with borrowed money.

203.title: On Day 1000, Sessions Says Senate Dems Forfeit Leadership Privilege For Refusal To Budget
203.description: WASHINGTON, January 25—As the nation marked the scandalous milestone of 1,000 days since Senate Democrats last authored and adopted a concurrent budget resolution, Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor to explain why a budget is so crucial, particularly in a time of fiscal distress.

204.title: Cornyn On FOX Ahead Of The 1000th Day Since Dems Passed A Budget
204.description: WASHINGTON, January 23—On FOX News this morning, Sen. John Cornyn pointed out that President Obama's State of the Union address tomorrow will coincide with the 1,000th day since Senate Democrats passed a budget. Last year the Democrats did not offer a budget at all, or even allow the Budget Committee to meet to work on a resolution. As Cornyn noted, "We've seen a 39 percent increase in the national debt since Obama has been President because Harry Reid will not allow a budget to come to the floor and be debated and passed."

205.title: Sessions: President Obama Is Shrinking Middle Class Opportunity
205.description: WASHINGTON, December 19--Ranking Member Sessions spoke on the Senate floor recently to outline the ways President Obama's policies are hurting the middle class and limiting opportunity for hardworking taxpayers, including in the areas of debt, health care, regulation, energy, trade, and illegal immigration.

206.title: Sessions On Fox: President's Policies Threaten The Middle Class
206.description: WASHINGTON, December 11—Ranking Member Sessions appeared on Fox News' "America's News HQ" today to discuss how President Obama's policies are hurting hardworking taxpayers, including on the issues of debt, energy, trade, and illegal immigration.

207.title: Greta Interviews Sessions On The President's Kansas Speech
207.description: WASHINGTON, December 8—Sen. Sessions appeared on FOX News' "On the Record" last night to discuss the president's latest political attack on Congressional Republicans. Sessions points out that despite his rhetoric and clever tactics, which sound and look strikingly similar to a campaign strategy, the president has never laid out a real, long-term plan for America's fiscal and economic future.

208.title: Sessions Responds To President's Kansas Speech, Says Hardworking Americans 'Entitled To Better'
208.description:
WASHINGTON, December 7—Responding to President Obama's Kansas speech, in which Obama re-pitched his economic vision, Sessions explained that: "We are on an unsustainable path, and I do not see in this speech today any commitment, any leadership from the president on this fundamental issue. And the most fundamental failure of his leadership is not to look the American people in the eye and tell them honestly and truthfully that we are spending too much."  Sessions continued: "We're told that the president cares about the middle class, and if you question any of these schemes, then you don't care about working Americans. I reject that. That's offensive to me...I love and respect the working people of this country, and they are entitled to better. They are entitled to leadership that tells them the truth, and the truth is we are endangering their future and their children's future by allowing the most incredible debt increases the nation has ever seen, and that has got to be brought under control."

To view Sessions statement, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/uOkd1O

209.title: Johnson Details New Fiscal Savings Proposal on FOX
209.description: WASHINGTON, December 1, 2011--Sen. Ron Johnson appeared on FOX's "Your World with Cavuto" to discuss the Implementation of Simpson-Bowles Spending Reductions Act that he introduced in the Senate. This legislation would save an estimated $655 billion over ten years by implementing several of the Simpson-Bowles debt commission's bipartisan spending recommendations: "A year ago the Simpson-Bowles commission issued their report and it really fell on deaf ears. I mean this President said he was going to work in the next year on making the tough choices, but he hasn't....The real problem we have is the president has not led."

210.title: Sessions Discusses Payroll Tax, War Gimmick To Conceal Deficit Spending
210.description:
WASHINGTON, December 2—Sen. Sessions spoke on the floor last night to express concerns over a proposal to cancel workers' payments into the Social Security Trust Fund, which serves as a retirement account for all Americans. Because that money will have to be made up for with new spending, the pension holiday would add $265 billion to the deficit.

Sessions also addressed the partial list of items that Congress is set to take up before the end of the year—which some have proposed paying for with a gimmick resulting from phony war savings: "We are going to deal with the alternative minimum tax. That is going to cost $50 billion. We are going to deal with unemployment insurance, an additional $70 billion to extend those payments beyond 90-some-odd weeks. We are going to fix the doctors payment, because we have to... $21 billion. We are going to extend most, if not all, of the tax extenders... $90 billion. The total is $500 billion...

Now I just heard... somebody said, 'Well, we're just going to count the savings from the war. The Congressional Budget Office will show the decline in expenses for the Iraq and Afghanistan wars will be a savings. We can just spend that.' That is fraudulent, that's a gimmick, and it should not be acceptable."

211.title: 'Special Report' On Disproportionate Defense Cuts
211.description: WASHINGTON, November 23—Last night on FOX News, "Special Report" aired a segment on defense cuts in the Budget Control Act—cuts that will now be automatically triggered by the supercommittee's failure to reach a deficit reduction agreement. The Budget Committee's Republican staff recently produced an analysis demonstrating the cuts would reduce only defense spending, while the other 5/6 of the budget would continue to surge. To view the full analysis, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/up7Bhz

212.title: Sessions Cites Gimmicks In Voting Against Spending Bill
212.description: WASHINGTON, November 17, 2011--Before a vote a 'minibus' appropriations bill, which included funding for Agriculture; Commerce, Justice, and Science; and Transportation-Housing and Urban Development, Sessions gave a floor speech objecting to gimmicks and spending increases contained in the legislation.  Despite claims that the bill would cut spending, it actually increased spending by approximately $9.4 billion.  In opposing the measure, Sessions described the bill as "a statement that Washington does not take seriously the extraordinary danger posed by our debt."

213.title: President Should Not Be Held To Lower Standard Than Mayors And Governors
213.description:
WASHINGTON, November 22, 2011--Senator Sessions appeared on CNN Newsroom today to discuss the failure of the supercommittee to reach an agreement.  Earlier in the year, House Republicans produced an historic long-term budget plan while Senate Democrats failed to produce one at all.
During the interview, Sessions remarked:
"It is amazing to me that the president would not be a leader and a player in this, I cannot imagine a mayor or a governor facing anything like this kind of debt threat not being engaged in any of the reform... he is not a player in the great debate of our time. There is no greater threat to America than this debt crisis and he has refused to look the American people in the eye and tell them how serious it is."

214.title: FOX Panel: Obama's Hands-Off Approach To Deficit Reduction Is A Campaign Strategy
214.description:
WASHINGTON, November 22—On Special Report last night, Charles Krauthammer and Bill Kristol discussed President Obama's lack of involvement in the supercommittee's negotiations, calling it a "total abdication of leadership on his part."

On Monday, the supercommittee announced it had failed to reach an agreement to reduce the deficit by the required $1.2 trillion. Although Press Secretary Jay Carney lamented that outcome, he said it was  "absolutely not" a problem for "him not to have been as involved" in the negotiations.

215.title: Sessions Explains Budget Gimmicks in Debt Deal
215.description: WASHINGTON, November 16—Speaking on the Senate floor today, Ranking Member Sessions addressed a gimmick in the Budget Control Act, the legislation that arose out of last summer's debt limit deal, that will imposed a discretionary spending cap of $1,054 billion—an increase over last year—rather than the $1,043 billion advertised. Additionally, the bill includes a little-discussed provision that removed the longstanding 60 vote threshold for designating emergency spending. As Sessions explained, "because the bill was rushed to passage in the 59th minute of the 11th hour, nobody knew the gimmick at the time."

216.title: Sessions On Debt Threat: Commander-In-Chief Absent From Battle
216.description:
WASHINGTON, November 21--In an interview on FOX's "America's Newsroom" this morning, Ranking Member Sessions discussed the lack of engagement from the President. Instead of becoming engaged in the supercommittee's efforts, the President has acted irresponsibly by removingh himself from the greatest problem our nation faces.  

Sessions explained, "I hear commentators saying, 'oh how clever the president is not to put his hands on this...' It's not clever; it's irresponsible, it's wrong, it's a failure of leadership, it's absent without leave... Can you imagine the greatest threat to our country, dwarfs any other problem this nation has... and the president's not providing any leadership? The commander-in-chief is absent from battle."

217.title: On Bloomberg, Sessions Reacts To Expected Supercommittee Failure
217.description:
WASHINGTON, November 21--In an interview on Bloomberg TV this morning, Ranking Member Sessions discussed the supercommittee and the news that the special panel is set to announce it has failed to reach an agreement to reduce the deficit.

Sessions reiterated his longstanding criticism of secret negotiations and backroom deals, noting that the Gang of Six and the talks led by Vice President Biden also failed this year when they were conducted behind closed doors. Sessions urged Congress to fulfill its responsibilities to the American people by publicly putting forward and debating a deficit-reduction plan that will change the U.S.' debt trajectory, as House Republicans did earlier this year. NOTE: It has now been 936 days since Senate Democrats have offered a budget plan, as required by law.

218.title: Sessions Criticizes Composition Of Sequester, Says Surging Domestic Spending Must Be Addressed
218.description: WASHINGTON, November 18, 2011--As the Senate began consideration on a bill to fund the Defense Department, Ranking Member Sessions cautioned against the disproportionately steep defense cuts that would take effect if the deficit reduction "supercommittee" fails to reach its targets. If that happened, automatic cuts would kick in that former Bush and Obama Defense Secretary Robert Gates warned would be "catastrophic" for our national security.

219.title: Johnson Discusses Supercommittee On FOX
219.description: In an interview on FOX, Senator Ron Johnson discussed the lack of engagement from the President in reducing the nation's debt.

220.title: Sessions Warns Of Possible Gimmicks In Supercommittee Product
220.description: WASHINGTON, November 17--Ranking Member Sessions delivered a speech on the Senate floor today to caution that any deficit-reduction plan offered by the so-called "supercommittee" must be honestly scrutinized to ensure it doesn't contain gimmicks that create the appearance of false savings. As Sessions noted, "what we've seen so far indicates that, secret deals, while they remain secret, are promoted to be far better than they are when you begin to see what's really in them. The devil will always be in the details."

221.title: Sessions Outlines Middle Class Agenda
221.description:
WASHINGTON, November 16--On the Senate floor this afternoon, Ranking Member Sessions confronted a gimmick from the Budget Control Act (the result of this summer's debt limit deal) that will result in more than $110 billion in spending over the next 10 years than the bill's proponents argued.

Although discretionary spending this year was supposed to be capped at $1,043 billion--$7 billion lower than last year's level--the Budget Control Act also created a new $11.3 billion "disaster" fund that is not included in the spending caps. As a result, total discretionary spending this year will be $1,054 billion rather than $1,050 billion.

Rather than increased spending through gimmicks that benefit the political class, Sessions urged adoption of a middle class agenda: "That means creating jobs through the private sector; producing more American energy—keeping our wealth at home. Making the government lean and productive—a servant of the American people. Confronting our dangerously rising debt, which threatens our economy and jobs; adopting a globally competitive tax code; upholding the rule of law in trade; eliminating unwise, damaging regulations; and finally delivering the good people of this country the honest and responsible budget they deserve."

222.title: CBO: President's "Stimulus" Hurts Long-Term Economic Growth
222.description:
WASHINGTON, November 15--In a Budget Committee hearing today, Congressional Budget Office Director Douglas Elmendorf admitted that his agency's long-term projections about President Obama's first stimulus bill show a negative long-term effect on economic growth.

As a centerpiece of his current economic agenda, the president is proposing a new, half-trillion dollar stimulus bill.

223.title: Bloomberg Questions Obama's Leadership On Deficit Reduction
223.description: WASHINGTON, November 8--New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg addressed the Center for American Progress today and suggested the president should be doing more to confront our nation's crippling debt. Bloomberg said that "the executive branch must do more than submit a plan to a committee and then step aside and hope the committee members take action. That is not how any CEO would run a business."

224.title: Sessions Remarks On Latest Vote On President's 2nd Stimulus
224.description:
WASHINGTON, November 3—Prior to a vote on the latest component of the president's second stimulus plan (which would increase the deficit by nearly $300 billion in this fiscal year alone), Sen. Sessions spoke on the floor to express his concerns with Democrat leaders' tax-and-spend mentality.

Sessions said: "This country is spending enough. We're wasting enough money now. It would be a mistake for the American people to allow Congress to extract more money from them to spend today on even a new program while we're doing nothing about the surging debt that's running on in our country. Nothing about the Solyndra-type loan programs that are wasting money in huge amounts."

Although each vote on the president's stimulus plan has received bipartisan opposition, the Senate's Democrat leaders continue to press for more spending that would be financed by large tax increases.

225.title: Senators Press For Repeal Of Gimmick-Laden Program From President's Healthcare Law
225.description:
WASHINGTON, November 3--On the Senate floor yesterday, Sen. Sessions joined his colleagues Senators John Thune, John McCain, and John Barrasso in attempting to repeal the CLASS Act, a long-term care program created as part of the president's health care law. Even HHS Secretary Kathleen Sebelius recently admitted there would be no way for her Department to make CLASS sustainable, adding to pressure to repeal the controversial program.

Sessions stated: "One of the greatest financial misrepresentations in history, if it continues to be on the books, will be the contention that this health care bill will actually create money for the United States Treasury."

226.title: FOX Interviews Sessions On 'Solyndra Rule,' Growing Concerns Of WH Corporate Favoritism
226.description:
WASHINGTON, November 2--On America's Newsroom this morning, Ranking Member Sessions discussed the latest round of questions regarding the Obama Administration's taxpayer-funded loan guarantees for green energy. Following the now-notorious case of Solyndra, a second clean energy company, Beacon Power, has filed for bankruptcy after receiving a $43 million loan guarantee from the Department of Energy. Sessions discussed the Solyndra Rule, which says that tax increases should not be put forward until the government has gotten rid of every instance of waste and abuse of taxpayer dollars.

Earlier, Sessions said in a statement that "the revelation that another corporation receiving a loan from the Obama administration has filed for bankruptcy is further evidence of the reckless abuse of taxpayers' dollars in the pursuit of green jobs." To view that statement, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/uVQkba.

227.title: FOX Airs Luntz Focus Group On Sessions' Honest Budget Act
227.description: WASHINGTON, November 2--Appearing on Neil Cavuto's show yesterday, Frank Luntz discussed Sen. Sessions' Honest Budget Act, a legislative package to put an end to Washington's most egregious budget gimmicks. To view additional information about the legislation, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/HonestBudgetAct

228.title: Sessions Outlines Spending Increases And Gimmicks In Appropriations Package
228.description:
WASHINGTON, November 1—Speaking on the Senate floor yesterday, Sen. Sessions outlined spending increases and budget gimmicks in the "minibus" appropriations bill currently pending in the Senate. 

While the Democrat majority contends that this spending package would save money, Sessions demonstrated that this is not so: "when discretionary and mandatory spending are scored on this bill, the overall spending compared to last year went up by $10 billion, or 4 percent. Relative to the amounts Senators were asked to approve for these three bills last year, we are being asked this year to increase spending—not decrease spending."

229.title: Sessions Announces Opposition To Controversial Budget Nominee
229.description:
WASHINGTON, October 20—Prior to the vote on Heather Higginbottom's nomination to be Deputy Director for the Office of Management and Budget, Sen. Sessions laid out his concerns with the nominee and urged his colleagues to oppose her. 

Sessions' objections centered on Ms. Higginbottom's lack of budget or finance experience and her unwillingness to honestly address questions about President Obama's budget submission. (To view Ms. Higginbottom's testimony before the Budget Committee, please click here: http://youtu.be/muXovEBakag.) In announcing his opposition, Sessions said, "Ms. Higginbottom's experience points to someone who has been on the wrong side, however, of fiscal restraint. Instead of crafting policies to decrease spending, she has been focused on new programs to increase spending."

The nominee was confirmed by a vote of 64-26.

230.title: Sessions Pushes Amendment To Fight Improper Use of Quadrupling Food Stamp Funds
230.description:
WASHINGTON, October 20—Speaking on the Senate floor yesterday evening, Sen. Sessions discussed his pending amendments to the appropriations package currently being considered in the Senate, including one to fight the mishandling of food stamp funds. This year's proposal calls for a 14 percent increase in food stamp funding, an increase that would bring the level to quadruple what it was in just 2001. Much of that money is going to individuals who would not ordinarily qualify for the benefit.  This is done through "categorical eligibility," a provision in current law that allows households that receive other federal benefits or assistance to automatically qualify for food stamps, in many cases regardless of their financial situation. Sessions' amendment would put an end to categorical eligibility, thus simply requiring recipients to meet the specific requirements set forth in the Food Stamp program.

Additionally, Sessions brought up several examples of improper use of the program, including one instance where a defendant in the notorious "Operation Fast and Furious" case received food stamps even as he was purchasing hundreds of illegal weapons. While Senate Democrats want to increase the programs funding to a level quadruple what it was in 2001, Sessions asked: "Shouldn't we first clean up our act before we demand the American people send more money up here? Until we do that, raising tax rates will only be funding the continued abuse of the American taxpayer."

231.title: Sessions Unveils Amendments To Combat Billions In Spending Through Waste, Gimmicks
231.description:
WASHINGTON, October 19—Speaking on the Senate floor last night, Sen. Sessions announced he would be introducing three amendments to put an end to billions in unnecessary spending through waste, fraud, abuse, and gimmicks. A summary of Sessions' amendments follows:

• Elimination of categorical eligibility for the food stamp program—Under current law, individuals often become automatically eligible for food stamps simply by receiving a separate government benefit—regardless of whether they meet specific food stamp eligibility requirements. As Sessions noted, "In one state... if a person uses a pregnancy hotline, apparently, their assets are overlooked and they can qualify for food stamps... In many states, all that is needed to become food stamp eligible is to be mailed a brochure by the government... regardless of the assets the individual might have."

• House of Representatives levels on food stamp funding—Senate Democrats propose an additional $9 billion in funding over last year's level, which would amount to a quadrupling ($20 billion to $80 billion) since 2001. Preventing this $9 billion increase would save nearly $100 billion over 10 years, assuming no other increases. The number of people using food stamps has increased seven-fold since the program's national expansion in the 1970s—with nearly 1 in 7 Americans now receiving benefits. Meanwhile, food stamp funds have been wasted, mishandled, and misused. In one notorious case, a defendant in the "Operation Fast and Furious" scandal was a food stamp recipient at the same time as he was buying more than 300 high-powered assault rifles and other weapons. In another case, a Michigan man was able to continue receiving food stamps after winning $2 million in a lottery because his winnings were counted as an asset rather than income.

• No CHiMPs that don't save money—This amendment would create a 60-vote point of order against any appropriations bill if it includes CHiMPs (changes in mandatory programs) that do not reduce outlays over the ten-year window. CHiMPs is a commonly used gimmick that has resulted in at least $72 billion in deficit spending since 2005.

232.title: Sessions Proposes The 'Solyndra Rule'
232.description:
WASHINGTON, October 18— Speaking on the Senate Floor today, Sen. Sessions offered several amendments to spending bills being considered that would save billions by confronting waste and budget gimmicks: http://1.usa.gov/nlgJ8r. 

In doing so, Sessions articulated the "Solyndra Rule" as a counter to the President's "Buffett Rule":

"President Obama has coined a term called the 'Buffett Rule' in his push to raise taxes. This rule relies on a little sleight-of-hand since Buffett pays mostly capital gains tax. The upper brackets, as we all know, pay the highest income tax rates. That's how our system works. But this debate about taxes is a little premature. That's why I would like to suggest something called the 'Solyndra Rule.' Under this rule, before any proposals are offered to raise taxes, we first put an end to the wasteful and inappropriate spending in Washington. Until we do, raising tax rates only funds Washington's continuing abuse of all American taxpayers."

233.title: Greta Interviews Thune On The Buffett Rule Act
233.description: Sen. John Thune joined FOX News' "On the Record" to discuss his recently introduced "Buffett Rule Act" to make it easier for those who believe they are not paying enough taxes to pay more to help pay down the federal debt. Unlike President Obama's tax-and-spend plan, the Buffett Rule Act would not increase taxes for job creators and small businesses.

234.title: Sessions Confronts 4 Persistent Myths About Defense Spending
234.description: WASHINGTON, October 7--In an address before the 2011 Values Voter Summit today, Ranking Member Sessions confronted the four most persistent myths about the Pentagon's budget and its contribution to the deficit. Sessions said that the Pentagon, like every other agency in the government, would have to tighten its belt, but that it should not bear disproportionately cuts that adversely impact military readiness and capabilities.

235.title: Greta Interviews Sessions On the Honest Budget Act
235.description:
WASHINGTON, October 6—Sen. Sessions appeared on FOX News' "On the Record" last night to present the details of the Sessions-Snowe Honest Budget Act, a plan unveiled yesterday to put an end to Washington's most dishonest budget gimmicks. As Greta noted, "Your Honest Budget Act would do away with all this stuff that's basically scamming the American people." Sessions agreed, pointing out that over the last five years, the gimmicks addressed in the bill have added at least $350 billion to the debt. Sessions also expressed optimism that there would be bipartisan support for his bill. 

For more information on the Honest Budget Act, including legislative text, specific examples, and detailed summaries, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/nlgJ8r.

236.title: Reid Blocks Vote On President's Stimulus Bill
236.description: WASHINGTON, October 4--This past weekend, President Obama remarked: "Now, you may have heard me say this a few times before -- I'll say it again: Pass the [stimulus] bill. Enough gridlock. Enough delay. Enough politics. Pass this bill." Today, Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell attempted to bring up that bill for a vote in the Senate, but Majority Leader Harry Reid objected to the request, suggesting that he had other, higher priorities that the Senate would consider first.

237.title: Sessions Urges Adoption Of Two-Year Budget Cycle
237.description:
WASHINGTON, October 4—The Senate Budget Committee held a hearing today to consider various reforms to the budget process, including a proposal that would switch to a two-year budget cycle (known as biennial budgeting) rather than the current annual budget cycle. Sen. Sessions spoke in strong support of this reform, arguing that it would allow Congress more time to fully and adequately exercise its oversight responsibilities and monitor federal spending.

Sessions has previously co-sponsored biennial budget proposals.

238.title: Buffett Declines To Support 'Buffett Rule' Or President's New Stimulus
238.description:
WASHINGTON, September 30--Today on CNBC, Warren Buffett declined on multiple occasions to offer his support for either the "Buffett Rule"--President Obama's plan to increase taxes on higher-income families--or the president's new stimulus package, which would increase federal borrowing by nearly half a trillion dollars.

Transcript follows (from Real Clear Politics):

CNBC: "Are you happy that the way it is being described. Is the program that the White House has presented a million dollars and over your program? "

Warren Buffett: "Well, the precise program which will -- I don't know what their program will be. My program would be on the very high incomes that are taxed very low. Not just high incomes. Somebody making $50 million a year playing baseball, his taxes won't change. Make $50 million a year appearing on television, his income won't change. But, if they make a lot of money and pay a very low tax rate, like me, it would be changed by a minimum tax that would only bring them up to what other people pay."

CNBC: "Does that mean you disagree with the president's new jobs proposal which would be paid for by raising taxes on households with incomes of over $250,000."

Buffett: "That's another program that I won't be discussing. My program is to have a tax on ultra-rich people who are very tax rates. Not just all rich people. It would probably apply to 50,000 people in a population of 300 million."

239.title: Sessions On FOX: In These Tough Economic Times, We Can't Let China 'Rig The Game'
239.description: Mike Emanuel of FOX News discusses the China currency bill that will be considered in the Senate during the week of October 3rd. Ranking Member Sessions is an original co-sponsor of the legislation.

240.title: On Senate Floor, Sessions Explains Gimmicks In President's Fiscal Plan
240.description: WASHINGTON, September 20— Speaking on the Senate Floor today, Sen. Sessions detailed the gimmicks in the president's fiscal plan, explaining that it "piles gimmick upon gimmick added up to little more than a tax hike camouflaged as fiscal restraint. Promised spending control is nowhere to be found." To view the Budget GOP Committee analysis revealing these conclusions, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/njKn93

241.title: Unmasking A Gimmick: Manipulating Data To Spur Higher Spending
241.description:
"That's unacceptable to me [to say that] we've got to scale back on the investments that have always helped our economy grow.  We've got to settle for second-rate roads and second-rate bridges and second-rate airports, and schools that are crumbling." - President Obama, remarks on economic growth and deficit reduction, September 19, 2011 (http://1.usa.gov/mSLqov)

President Obama and Democrat leaders, including Budget Committee Chairman Kent Conrad, have repeatedly called this year for increased "investments"—federal spending—in "education, innovation, clean energy, and infrastructure". Implicit (and in some cases explicit) in their calls is the argument that such spending has fallen off in recent years. But is this the case?

242.title: Sessions Rebukes White House For Bogus Accounting: "America Deserves An Honest Budget"
242.description: WASHINGTON, September 20--- At today's Senate Budget Committee hearing, Sen. Sessions conveyed his displeasure with the White House's release of the president's fiscal plan: "consider the astounding disparity between the levels of taxation claimed verses those actually contained in the proposal. The White House asserts $2 in cuts for every $1 in tax hikes. There is not a single penny of net spending that's cut."

243.title: Sessions' Opening Statement Details Inaccuracies In President's Plan
243.description: WASHINGTON, September 20—At a hearing today in the Budget Committee, Sen. Sessions delivered an opening statement to lay out his concerns with the deficit plan that the president presented yesterday. A Budget Committee staff analysis (http://1.usa.gov/qjrnOP) found that total deficit reduction is only $1.4 trillion, less than half what the White House had claimed. What's more, the deficit reduction relies entirely on tax increases, and net federal spending will actually increase rather than decrease.

244.title: Thune: President's Proposal Opposite Of What Is Needed To Create Jobs
244.description: WASHINGTON, September 20-- On America's Newsroom this morning, Sen. John Thune expressed his concerns with the president's recently unveiled deficit plan. Sen. Thune focused his criticism on the president's $1.5 trillion tax hike, noting the president has previously declared that "you don't raise taxes in the middle of a recession."

245.title: Johnson: Burdensome Federal Regulations Cost Us Jobs Every Year
245.description: WASHINGTON, September 15--Senator Ron Johnson appeared on FOX's Cavuto today to discuss the Regulation Moratorium and Jobs Preservation Act of 2011 that he authored (Ranking Member Sessions is a co-sponsor). The bill would prohibit agencies from taking significant regulatory action until unemployment falls below 7.8%. Johnson explained that it costs small businesses $1.75 trillion a year to comply with federal regulations, which equals 12 percent of the American economy.

246.title: Sessions Says Reid's FEMA Bill Requires Scrutiny
246.description: WASHINGTON, September 15--With the Senate currently considering a disaster relief funding bill that is nearly $2 billion more than even what the White House requested, Sen. Sessions took to the Senate floor today to discuss the Senate's proper role in managing the people's money.

247.title: Democrat And Republican Experts Agree: Pursue Policies That Spur Growth Without Adding Debt
247.description:
WASHINGTON, September 15--At today's Budget Committee hearing, Ranking Member Sessions asked each of the three witnesses (Dr. Mark Zandi of Moody's Analytics, Dr. Chad Stone of the Center for Budget and Policy Priorities, and Dr. Kevin Hassett of the American Enterprise Institute) for their views on a series of policy proposals.

Each of the witnesses agreed without equivocation that reforming the tax code, reducing burdensome regulations, and developing more American energy would lead to economic growth without adding to the deficit.

248.title: Zandi Says No Deficit Reduction Until "After The Election"
248.description: WASHINGTON, September 15—Dr. Mark Zandi of Moody's Analytics testified today before the Budget Committee, where he made the claim there should be no further deficit reduction "until after the election."

249.title: Sessions Delivers Opening Statement At First Senate Budget Hearing In Six Months
249.description: WASHINGTON, September 15—Sen. Sessions delivered an opening statement today at the first hearing in the Democrat-led Senate Budget Committee in 182 days (by contrast, the Republican House Budget Committee has held 9 hearings during that time). Sessions also alluded to the decision of Senate Democrats not to present a budget at all this year: "The fact that our nation continues to operate without a budget plan lies at the heart of our current economic crisis. America desperately needs the confidence and predictably that only a concrete fiscal plan can provide. The budget process isn't broken—Washington has simply abandoned it."

250.title: President's Budget Office Fails To Provide Crucial Info On Stimulus II
250.description:
WASHINGTON, September 14—Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today to address the president's repeated calls for Congress to pass the Administration's so-called jobs bill. In fact, President Obama has used the phrase "pass this bill" 90 times in the last week. But despite this seeming urgency, the Administration failed to submit any sort of price tag or tables showing the plan's budgetary impact.

Sessions also discussed his letter to OMB Director Jack Lew requesting this information, but noted he has yet to receive a response. To view that letter, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/ntf4O6

251.title: Sessions: President's 2nd Stimulus Would Wipe Out Savings From Debt Limit Agreement
251.description: WASHINGTON, September 13—Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor yesterday address the president's jobs and spending plan, submitted to Congress yesterday evening. Although the Congressional Budget Office has not yet been able to score the plan, it is estimated that it will cost nearly half a trillion dollars—yet the Obama Administration failed to provide the promised details about how the plan would be paid for. Sessions also questioned the logic of spending and borrowing more government money in an effort to artificially stimulate the economy: "Day after day, week after week, we have increased spending in this country to the point that it cannot be sustained."

252.title: President's New Stimulus Would Wipe Out Savings From Debt Ceiling Deal
252.description: WASHINGTON, September 9 -- Sen. Sessions appeared on FOX's America's Newsroom today to further respond to the president's jobs speech and to his call for additional stimulus spending. Sessions urged President Obama to refocus his attention on measures that would create jobs without adding to the deficit, including the production of more American energy, a reduction of regulations, and a streamlining of the tax code to make American businesses more competitive.

253.title: Sessions On President's Speech: Government Stimulus Has Been Tried, Failed
253.description:
WASHINGTON, September 9 -- Sen. Sessions appeared last night on CNN's "Piers Morgan Tonight" to discuss President Obama's address to Congress, which the president used as an opportunity to call for more stimulus spending. 

Sessions noted that economists have told us that "the debt itself that is destroying our economy," yet the president continues to call for more spending that would have to be paid for with borrowed money.

254.title: Sessions To President: The Debt Crisis Is A Jobs Crisis
254.description:
WASHINGTON, September 7--Today on the Senate floor, Sen. Sessions spoke about President Obama's upcoming jobs address and explained what he thought an adequate speech would be. Sessions noted that the president has yet to put forward any concrete budget or spending plan other than his February budget, which was voted down 97-0. Sessions stressed that any new proposals from the president would need to be submitted in detailed, concrete form for review by the public, the press, and the Congress.

As the Ranking Member said, "the rhetoric needs to confront reality. The president has given a number of speeches about creating jobs and reducing the deficit, but a speech is no substitute for a budget or for a detailed plan... I know the pressure is on to just do something so you can politically say you did something, but that's not sufficient now. We need mature, strong, detailed leadership--a detailed plan that would put us on a path to a sound economy."

255.title: Ingraham Takes Dems To Task Over Lack Of Budget
255.description: On the O'Reilly Factor, guest host Laura Ingraham pressed Democratic strategist Bernard Whitman and Rep. Charles Rangel (D-NY15) over the Democrat Congress' failure to pass a budget in over 840 days: "We have 9.2 percent unemployment, and you [the president and congressional Democrats] had two years to pass a budget and couldn't do it."

256.title: FOX: Sessions Says President Is In Denial On Spending
256.description: On America Live, Megyn Kelly discussed President Obama's call for a second "stimulus," and noted that Sen. Sessions has said the president is "in denial" about the need to bring spending under control. Over the first two years of President Obama's term, domestic spending has increased by 24 percent. But despite historic budget deficits, his budget submission for the next fiscal year called for spending increases of 8, 10, or even 62 percent for some agencies.

257.title: STOSSEL: U.S. Should Learn From Canada's Experience In Cutting Spending
257.description: FOX News host John Stossel speaks with Hoover Institute economist David Henderson about Canada's experience reducing its deficits in the 1990s. As the Canadian government cut government spending, the nation's deficits dropped sharply and even turned to surpluses. Meanwhile, Canada reduced the size of its government workforce but actually saw its unemployment rate fall; that rate remains well below the U.S.' jobless rate. Thanks to these positive steps, Canada's dollar appreciated as investors gained confidence in the state of the government's finances.

258.title: President's Own Fiscal Commission Co-Chair Says Obama Must Give Specifics
258.description:
Today on FOX News, Alan Simpson, former co-chair of the president's fiscal commission, suggested that voters who are frustrated with the lack of meaningful action on deficit reduction should demand that politicians put forward specific plans for how they would address different budgetary challenges.

NOTE: While the Republican House wrote and passed a budget earlier this year, Senate Democrats have refused to put a budget plan on paper at all this year, or pass one in more than 830 days. President Obama, meanwhile, rejected the findings of his own fiscal commission, put forward a budget that was rejected 97-0, and later gave a speech that was so lacking in detail the Congressional Budget Office was forced to point out that "we don't estimate speeches."

259.title: Kristol And Krauthammer: Obama Failing To Lead By Demagoguing Debt Downgrade
259.description: On FOX's "Special Report" last night, Bill Kristol and Charles Krauthammer sharply criticized President Obama for his lack of leadership on the debt ceiling and his efforts to shift blame for the U.S.' credit rating downgrade. As the commentators point out, the president got the long-term debt-limit extension he asked for, but the U.S. was still downgraded because the package proved to be too small to meaningfully change the nation's debt trajectory. They also noted that the president and congressional Democrats have consistently refused to put any serious plans for dealing with the debt on paper.: "He has put nothing on the table and he blames everybody else."

260.title: Sessions Debates Credit Downgrade On ABC's 'This Week': President In Denial
260.description:
Sen. Sessions appeared on ABC's 'This Week' with Christiane Amanpour to debate the recent downgrade of America's credit rating from S&P, as well as the nation's growing fiscal crisis. Sessions debated Maryland Governor Martin O'Malley, chairman of the Democratic Governors Association. During the interview, Sessions warned against tax increases, saying that spending has surged dramatically under the president and "we've got to bring spending down, not increase the burden on the private sector." 

He also explained the adverse affects our debt was having on our economy: "The debt is now 100 percent of GDP, which is hammering our economy... that's why we're having the unexpected decline in growth that we've seen the first half of this year."

Sessions said that despite this fact that is supported by much academic research, the president remains in denial, and must rally the country behind needed reform: "When you have a Democratic Senate that will not produce a budget - 830 days without a budget - a president who submitted the most irresponsible budget in history, who is continuing to talk about spending and investing more, whose secretary of education was demanding a 13% increase in the department of education next fiscal year, beginning October 1st, you know we're in denial ; we are not understanding the threat."

"The president is going to have to look the American people in the eye and tell them we are on an unsustainable course... And if he asks us to reduce spending by 10% across the board, all departments and agencies, Congress would rally to him in a bipartisan way. But if he's going to deny we have a crisis, he's not going to have bipartisan support."

261.title: Sessions Responds To President's Call For More Spending After Debt Deal
261.description: AUGUST 3, WASHINGTON--Following the passage of the debt limit increase bill yesterday, President Obama spoke at a press conference where he continued to call for additional "investments," a phrase he has used many times to refer to spending increases. Sen. Sessions then spoke on the Senate floor to respond to the president's speech.

262.title: Majority Leader Calls Election Of Tea Party Members "Unfair To American People"

263.title: Piers Morgan Interviews Sessions On Debt Vote
263.description:
AUGUST 1, WASHINGTON--Sen. Sessions appeared on CNN's "Piers Morgan Tonight" to discuss his announcement that he would be voting against the debt limit increase.

Said Sessions: "I have decided I will not vote for the bill, although I really respect the people who have worked on it and the fact that it does make some real progress towards reducing spending, [albeit] far less than we need. But as the Ranking Republican on the Budget Committee, they put in language that really undermines our ability to even have a budget next year. It would be the third consecutive  year without a budget. So for me, that was a defining moment."

Sessions also confronted the suggestion that the Tea Party movement somehow refused to compromise, noting that the original House-passed budget cut far more than the spending cuts the House finally agreed to in an effort to produce a bill that could pass the Senate. Sessions said, "I think the Tea Party movement represented a spontaneous American expression of shock and concern over the spending that was going on in Washington. Members of Congress cannot possibly justify that they are borrowing 42 cents of every dollar that's spent. This is irresponsible. So they demanded change and elected a lot of new people. They've been called 'terrorists'; I would just say they put some terror in the hearts of big spenders."

264.title: Sessions Announces Opposition To Debt Limit Deal
264.description:
AUGUST 1, WASHINGTON--Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor tonight to announce his opposition to the debt limit deal set to be voted on in the Senate tomorrow.

Although Sessions acknowledged that the spending cuts contained in the package represent a modest step in the right direction, he laid out serious concerns with the legislation, including:

* The fact that the bill was first introduced at 3 a.m. this morning, yet will be voted on by noon tomorrow--leaving little time to review or even read the bill

* The bill "deems" budget resolutions for the next two years, effectively allowing Senate Democrats to continue ignoring their basic, statutory responsibility to pass a budget plan for the nation

* The bill sets up a special joint committee that will recommend a deficit reduction package that can only be debated for a short time, and cannot be amended.

265.title: Johnson On Greta To Lay Out Concerns With Debt Deal
265.description: AUGUST 1, WASHINGTON--Sen. Ron Johnson appeared on FOX News' "On the Record" last night to lay out his objections to the deficit reduction deal that was negotiated to raise the nation's debt ceiling.

266.title: Greta Interviews Sessions As Late-Hour Deficit Reduction Deal Is Announced
266.description:
JULY 31, WASHINGTON—Sen. Sessions appeared on a special edition of FOX News' "On the Record with Greta Van Susteren" tonight to react to the announcement that congressional leaders had reached a deal on a plan to increase the nation's borrowing authority.

Sessions noted that the plan contained spending reductions that only occurred as a result of the historic 2010 election, but noted that far more work remains to be done. Sessions, like many other Republicans, raised concerns about the negotiating process in Washington: "I've said that we need seven days to review this bill. We've known this day was coming for six months."

NOTE: It has now been 823 days since the Democrat-controlled Senate last passed a budget.

267.title: Senior Senate Dem Gets Law Wrong Trying To Explain Missing Budget
267.description:
JULY 31, WASHINGTON--In an interview today on "FOX News Sunday," Senate Majority Whip Dick Durbin  falsely claimed that Democrats have not passed a budget in 823 days because they have been unable to muster 60 votes for passage.

Durbin's claim is incorrect for three reasons. First, budget law states that budget resolutions are privileged, meaning they cannot be filibustered, only require a simple majority vote for passage, and can be brought up by the majority party (which controls the Senate floor schedule) at any time. Second, for a large portion of last year, Democrats controlled 60 seats in the Senate, and still chose not to pass a budget plan for the nation. Finally, Senate Democrats have not even written or introduced a budget plan this year, much less passed one out of the Senate.

268.title: Sessions: Any Debt Limit Deal Is "Only The First Step" To Changing Our Debt Trajectory
268.description:
JULY 31, WASHINGTON--Sen. Sessions appeared on FOX's "America's News HQ" today to discuss the debt limit and the competing proposals to increase the debt limit (shortly after the interview concluded, Sessions joined 48 other Senators in opposing the plan offered by Majority Leader Harry Reid. That plan was unable to even get majority support, failing by a vote of 50-49.).

Sessions also pointed out how much the House of Representatives has compromised this year--after originally passing a budget with over $6 trillion in spending cuts, the House's debt limit proposal cut just $1 trillion in an effort to win support in the Democrat-controlled Senate.

269.title: Krugman: "We Shouldn't Even Be Talking About Spending Cuts At All"
269.description: JULY 31, WASHINGTON--On ABC's "This Week" today, Paul Krugman illustrated why it's so difficult to cut spending in Washington: the progressive philosophy is that even when 40 cents of every dollar the federal government spends is borrowed, the answer is to spend and borrow more money.

270.title: Washington's Big Spenders Vilify Tea Party For Urging Fiscal Discipline
270.description:
JULY 31, WASHINGTON—Speaking on the Senate floor last night, Sen. Sessions explained that members of the Tea Party and their supporters "understand an important fact: This Congress is spending too much money. They are exactly correct in that regard. No Member of the United States Congress can, with clear conscience, look their constituents in the eye and say we have managed their money wisely."

The federal government currently borrows 40 cents of every dollar it spends, yet even the modest cuts most recently proposed by the Republican-led House have been met with stiff resistance by Washington's "big spenders." Senate Democrats and the White House haven't presented a real plan to cut spending all year, even after surging it so dramatically since 2008 (our gross debt will soon be as large as the entire economy, undermining economic confidence, stability, and growth).

271.title: Barrasso: The Debt, Not The Debt Ceiling, Is The Real Problem
271.description: JULY 30, WASHINGTON--Sen. John Barrasso spoke on the Senate floor tonight to address the debt ceiling negotiations and the Senate's failure to adopt a budget in 822 days.

272.title: Rubio: With No Budget In 822 Days, Dem Leaders Try To Force Last-Minute Debt Vote
272.description:
JULY 31, WASHINGTON--Sen. Marco Rubio spoke on the Senate floor last night to discuss the Senate's budget delay. While the House of Representatives has now passed three separate plans to change the nation's debt trajectory and deal with the debt limit deadline, the Democrat-controlled Senate has refused to pass a budget in over two years, and has not presented one at all this year.

Rubio said that "this has been the plan all along, by the way. The plan all along was not to take a position, to let the days count down until we got to this point with 72 hours to go, and then force a vote on something that they wanted... You want to know why people all across America get grossed out by politics? It's by watching this kind of stuff happen."

273.title: On MSNBC's Morning Joe, Sessions Debates Debt Limit
273.description:
On MSNBC's "Morning Joe," Sen. Sessions explained that the only reason we find ourselves in 11th hour without agreed upon legislation to address the debt and debt limit is because regular legislative process had been eschewed by the Democrat-led Senate and the White House : "At the last minute, as I predicted, we'll have all kinds of complex legislation and wheeling and dealing in an attempt to avoid a crisis and we should have dealt with it weeks, months ago." The Democrat-led Senate hasn't passed a budget in more than 800 days. 

Sessions also addressed the issue of taxes and job creation, saying: "I believe most Americans are skeptical about the idea that you tax the economy and create government jobs and this makes america a better place. They are skeptical about a bigger, ever-growing government."

274.title: Toomey And Ayotte: Senate Continues To Block Measures To Deal With Debt Crisis
274.description:
JULY 29, WASHINGTON--Senators Pat Toomey and Kelly Ayotte appeared on "Hannity" to discuss the debt limit negotiations and Majority Leader Harry Reid's refusal to bring up his bill for a vote on the Senate floor. Although Republicans had offered to allow a vote on the Reid debt limit proposal--which is expected to fail--the Majority Leader insisted on postponing the vote until 1:00 a.m. Sunday morning.

The Senators also observed that the House of Representatives has now passed three measures to address our debt crisis: the House Republican budget, the Cut Cap and Balance bill, and the Boehner debt limit proposal. The Senate, on the other hand, has yet to pass any such bill, and has refused to pass a budget now for 822 days.

275.title: Sessions Criticizes Obama For Saying Debt Limit Must Extend Past Election
275.description:
JULY 30, WASHINGTON--Sen. Sessions explained that the House-passed debt limit measure includes far fewer spending cuts than Republicans enacted in their previous budget plans--an effort to find a level of spending the Democrat-led Senate would actually be willing to cut. The Boehner legislation was the third major debt proposal to be passed by the House, only for the Senate to immediately table.

Sessions demanded: "We are going to work to get the [spending] numbers down and we're not going to wait two years after some convenient or inconvenient election."

276.title: Reid Objects To Consideration Of His Own Debt Bill
276.description:
JULY 29, WASHINGTON--Although Majority Leader Reid earlier today said that "time is short, and too much is at stake to waste even one more minute," he objected this evening to holding a vote to consider his own debt limit proposal.

Reid argued that his bill should be subject to a 51-vote threshold rather than the 60 votes traditionally required for significant pieces of legislation, although Reid himself has previously agreed with this important precedent  ("The need to muster 60 votes in order to terminate Senate debate naturally frustrates the majority and oftentimes the minority... But I recognize this requirement is a tool that serves the long-term interest of the Senate and the American people and our country.")

NOTE: Holding the vote 30 hours later, as the Democrats have insisted, is not expected to change the outcome.

To view Sen. Sessions' earlier floor speech on the various debt limit increase bills, please click here: http://youtu.be/52JDl05HvIM  To view a letter from all Budget Committee Republicans raising concerns about a specific provision in the Reid bill, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/q4EuMz

277.title: Sessions: "The President Thinks It's All About Him"
277.description:
JULY 29, WASHINGTON—Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor this morning to discuss the debt negotiations and the debt plan offered by Majority Leader Harry Reid, which President Obama has said he supports.

Sessions began, "The president said--really--this is what the president said a week ago: 'The only bottom line that I have is that we extend this debt ceiling through the next election, until 2013.' The president thinks this is about him. It's all about him. This is about America, and what's good for this country. It's not about the president. It's not about politics."

Sessions also revealed that a little-noticed provision in the Reid plan would "deem" budget resolutions to be passed for the next two years, further abrogating the statutory budget process that Senate Democrats have ignored for the past 821 days. Sessions asked: "Does the president think the Senate should go two more years without crafting or passing a budget? We've already gone two."

278.title: Sessions: Tea Party Didn't Start This Fire - They Sounded the Alarm
278.description:
In his speech on the Senate floor, Sessions stood up for the Tea Party and those who share their concerns: "You'll forgive me if I'm a little concerned by all these attacks on the Tea Party. They didn't start this fire—they sounded the alarm. Before the last election, when Democrats controlled both chambers of Congress by substantial majorities, every conversation was about increasing spending...
But, after the 2010 election, and the emergence of the Tea Party... we have finally begun to look at Washington's spending problem. Now, instead of just raising the debt ceiling with no spending cuts—as the White House initially and repeatedly demanded—we're talking about how to cut some spending."

279.title: Sessions: Senate Dems, WH Broke The Budget Process And Now We're Paying The Price
279.description:
JULY 28, WASHINGTON—On the Senate floor this afternoon, Sen. Sessions addressed the competing debt limit proposals offered by Speaker Boehner and Majority Leader Reid. Sessions noted that "if the year had begun with a serious budget proposal from the president, we wouldn't be in this mess right now...Senate Democrats, meanwhile, have refused to pass a budget in 820 days."

While Speaker Boehner's proposal cuts spending and raises the debt limit by roughly $1 trillion each, the debt proposal offered by Sen. Reid uses accounting tricks to hike the debt limit by $3 trillion while only cutting spending by a third as much. If enacted, Sen. Reid's proposal would represent the largest debt limit increase in U.S. history.

280.title: Sessions and Thune On Hannity: Democrats Have Resisted Spending Cuts Every Step Of The Way
280.description: JULY 27, WASHINGTON—Sen. Sessions appeared on "Hannity" last night alongside Sen. John Thune to discuss the latest in the debt negotiations. Thune pointed out the real reason why this process has come down to the last minute: Senate Democrats have refused to put forth a budget in 819 days, refused to bring Cut, Cap, and Balance up for a vote, and are once again waiting on House Republicans to bring the Boehner debt plan up for a vote. Sessions added: "the problem is, our Senate colleagues and the president want to tax more and spend more, not less. They're rejecting anything you send toward them that actually reduces spending and changes the debt course of America."

281.title: Sessions On Greta: Debt Deadline Nears But Dems Offer Phony Cuts, Obama Offers None
281.description: JULY 26, WASHINGTON—Sen. Sessions appeared on FOX News' "On the Record with Greta Van Susteren" last night to discuss the debt limit plan introduced by Sen. Harry Reid, and to reiterate his concerns about the last-minute nature of the negotiations. Sessions said he doubted Reid's plan would be voted out of the Senate because it cuts far less than advertised—only $1 trillion in exchange for a $3 trillion debt increase—and called on the president to reveal any plan he may have: "So the president doesn't have a $3 trillion plan, not a real plan that could score his $3 trillion. If he did, he would produce it. I invite him to produce it."

282.title: Reid's Gimmicks Unmasked: Record $3T Debt Increase Tied To Just $1T In Cuts
282.description:
JULY 26, WASHINGTON--After the Budget Committee's Republican analysts conducted a careful review of Majority Leader Reid's debt limit proposal, Sen. Sessions shared his findings on the Senate floor. 

The truth: Reid's proposal cuts only $1 trillion in spending for a nearly $3 trillion increase in the debt limit, and is based on an outdated spending baseline. This faulty baseline permitted Reid to temporarily disguise his irresponsible spending increases.

283.title: Sessions Warns Of Gimmicks In Reid Debt Bill
283.description:
JULY 26, WASHINGTON -- In a speech on the Senate floor last night, Sen. Sessions raised concerns about the gimmicks in Majority Leader Harry Reid's debt plan, unveiled "at the 11th hour and 50th minute," suggesting that the true level of spending cuts may be half of what the Majority Leader claims. Sessions has been calling for months for the products of closed-door debt negotiations to be made available in legislative text for review by Members of Congress, the media, and the American public.

Sessions noted: "Majority Leader Reid told us of his plan this afternoon and he told us not to worry, he has a 1-page summary. 'Trust us.... Just do what I tell you and go along and mind your manners and we will get this thing taken care of. Trust me.'  Well, the American people have been trusting Washington too long."

284.title: Grassley To Washington Democrats: More Than 800 Days Later, Where's Your Plan?
284.description: JULY 21, WASHINGTON -- Sen. Chuck Grassley took to the Senate floor today to continue the debate on the Republican "Cut, Cap, and Balance" plan: "I say to my colleagues: If you do not support this plan, then offer your own plan. You know the debt limit must be increased, but you also know we must take action to reduce the future levels of deficits and begin to bring our debt down. Where is your plan to do that? Where is your budget resolution that has not been presented in the last 800 or more days to the Senate, violating the budget law?"

285.title: Sessions And Lee Take Dem Leadership To Task For Shutting Down Senate, Nixing Debate
285.description:
JULY 22, WASHINGTON--In a spirited exchange last night, Sen. Sessions and Utah Sen. Mike Lee called out Majority Leader Harry Reid for scheduling and then cancelling weekend budget work in the Senate. The upper chamber had been set to vote on Saturday on the Cut, Cap, and Balance Act (legislation that a new CNN poll revealed that almost 2/3 of the country supports), but Sen. Reid moved to table the bill and go home for the weekend.

With just 11 days until the August 2 deadline, President Obama and the Democrat-led Senate have yet to reveal a plan of their own as spending and doubt continue to mount. In fact, Senate Democrats have refused to pass a budget for 814 days now. The Cut, Cap, and Balance bill remains the only plan that exists in legislative form to raise the debt limit. The legislation would cut current spending, cap future spending, and calls for a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution. It recently passed the House of Representatives with a strong bipartisan vote of 234-190.

Link to CNN poll: http://bit.ly/oP16F6

286.title: The House Unites For Cut, Cap, And Balance
286.description: JULY 22, WASHINGTON--As the Democrats continue to clamor for tax hikes, House Majority Whip Kevin McCarthy explained to Hannity last night the need for the Senate to support the Cut, Cap, and Balance Act, which passed the House with a bipartisan vote earlier this week. McCarthy made clear that Congress has been granted a second chance to pass a Balanced Budget Amendment and that it should not be voted down by a Democrat Senate that has yet to produce any plan of its own.

287.title: Barrasso: Dem Leadership Worried About Growing Support For Cut, Cap, Balance
287.description: JULY 21, WASHINGTON--As momentum built for the Republican "Cut, Cap, Balance" plan, Sen. John Barrasso appeared on "Your World" with Neil Cavuto to highlight the fact that no other Democrat proposals exist, either from the Senate or from President Obama.

288.title: The Truth: Sessions Unravels Fiction From White House On Debt
288.description:
JULY 21, WASHINGTON--In a forceful speech on the Senate floor today, Sen. Sessions pushed back on a number of Democrat myths about our nation's debt and deficits:

1. That the president has a $4 trillion deficit reduction plan
2. That the Iraq and Afghan wars and the Bush tax cuts are the major drivers of our debt
3. That the Gang of Six budget outline is a concrete plan that reduces the deficit $4 trillion - and doesn't raise taxes
4. That $2 trillion in spending cuts over 10 years -- the apparent ceiling for Democrats -- is enough to solve our fiscal crisis.

289.title: Cornyn: Cut, Cap, And Balance "Real Savings, Not Smoke And Mirrors"
289.description: JULY 21, WASHINGTON -- Sen. John Cornyn spoke on the Senate floor today to support the Cut, Cap, and Balance Act and to urge his colleagues in the Senate to do the same when the plan comes to a vote. It has been 812 days since Senate Democrats have passed a budget plan for the nation, and at the same time President Obama has refused to put any concrete plan on paper. Cornyn noted that Cut, Cap, Balance is the only debt limit proposal that has been revealed publicly and put in legislative form.

290.title: Tax Hikes Pushed by White House Would Harm Middle Class, Excuse Wasteful Spending
290.description:
JULY 20, WASHINGTON -- Sen. Sessions and Finance Committee Ranking Member Orrin Hatch participated in a colloquy on the Senate floor today to call attention the red herrings in Democrats' tax proposals. While President Obama and Democrat leaders have tried to claim that jet and yacht taxes are needed to close our deficits, the Senators pointed out that wasteful Washington spending has driven our debt to a level that can't be addressed simply by eliminating deductions.

In the first two years of the Obama administration, non-defense discretionary spending has surged by 24 percent. In President Obama's proposed budget, which remains the only concrete plan he's put on paper, the federal government is projected to spend $46 trillion over the next decade.

291.title: Ayotte And Thune: Budget Crisis Calls For Common-Sense Solution
291.description: JULY 21, WASHINGTON -- In a colloquy on the Senate floor, Sen. Ayotte joined Sen. Thune to call on the Senate to support the "Cut, Cap, and Balance" plan that the House passed last night. The Senators also discussed the need to balance the budget in order to get the United States on a responsible fiscal path.

292.title: Thune On Greta To Discuss Gang Of Six, Cut Cap And Balance
292.description:
JULY 21, WASHINGTON--Sen. John Thune, Chairman of the Republican Policy Committee, appeared on FOX News' "On the Record with Greta Van Susteren" last night to discuss the Republican "Cut, Cap, and Balance" plan, which would reduce current government spending, cap future spending, and calls for a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution in exchange for an increase in the debt limit.

Thune also addressed the Gang of Six outline that was released earlier this week. He congratulated his Senate colleagues on their work, but noted that many questions remain unanswered because no legislative text has yet been released.

293.title: Gang Of Six, President Still Have No Concrete Legislative Plan To Deal With Debt
293.description:
JULY 21, WASHINGTON -- On America's Newsroom this morning, Sen. Sessions continued to raise concerns about the Gang of Six outline, which he called "the suggestion of the day." Without legislative text that can be scored and analyzed, Sessions said, the draft proposal is little more than talking points that appear to call for tax hikes of between $1-$2 trillion.

Sessions also pushed back against Sen. Conrad's suggestion that the Gang's plan effectively broadens the base and reduces rates (in other words, that it eliminates deductions to pay for a lowering of marginal rates). Said Sessions: "Simplifying and reducing rates is a good goal. But it's hard to say you're reducing rates when you acknowledge that net taxes are going to go up $1 trillion over what's being paid today. So that's the little gamesmanship."

294.title: Toomey: Cut, Cap, And Balance Only Viable Plan To Confront Debt Crisis
294.description: JULY 20, WASHINGTON -- Sen. Pat Toomey appeared on the Sean Hannity show on Tuesday to discuss the House vote on the Cut, Cap, and Balance Act, which passed by a bipartisan vote of 234-190, and now awaits a vote in the Senate. Neither Senate Democrats nor President Obama has yet to release a concrete legislative plan to deal with the looming debt limit deadline.

295.title: Leadership On Debt Crisis Requires Concrete Plan
295.description: JULY 20, WASHINGTON -- While the Republicans have put their plan on the table to deal with our mounting spending and debt, President Obama still has yet to reveal any concrete proposal from the debt limit negotiations. The Gang of Six recently unveiled their outline, but as Sen. Sessions has pointed out, the lack of legislative text makes it difficult to know whether the Gang's cuts are real or how large the tax increases will be.

296.title: Vitter Unveils Measure To Limit Spending Without A Budget
296.description: JULY 19, WASHINGTON--Sen. Vitter spoke on the Senate floor today to discuss his efforts to prevent the Senate from appropriating money until it passes a budget resolution. Congress is required by law to adopt a budget each year, but it has now been 811 days since the Democrat-controlled Senate has done so.

297.title: Johnson: Debt Deal Requires Public Process, Not More Closed Meetings At White House
297.description: JULY 19, WASHINGTON -- On Morning Joe today, Senator Ron Johnson chided President Obama for not having been engaged in the process of debt negotiations, and urged that the results of those meetings be made available for public review.

298.title: Broken Promises: White House Claims Of Deficit Reduction Have Never Held Up
298.description:
JULY 18, WASHINGTON--On several Sunday shows this last weekend, OMB Director Jack Lew continued to make questionable claims about President Obama's deficit reduction goals.

Previously, under testimony before the Budget Committee, Director Lew attempted to characterize President Obama's formal budget submission--the only concrete plan the president has put forward--as being a responsible attempt to confront our nation's deficits and debt. Ranking Member Sessions then confronted Director Lew over the White House's misleading claims. (http://youtu.be/rTuzmyMwH7E)

299.title: Kristol: Only Republicans Have Public Debt Plan
299.description:
JULY 18, WASHINGTON—On FOX News Sunday yesterday, Bill Kristol pointed out that, unlike Republicans, President Obama and Congressional Democrats have not put a single debt plan on paper.  Kristol expressed his dissatisfaction with the White House's closed-door approach and challenged Senate Democrats to hold a vote on Republicans 'cat, cap, balance proposal' and to either offer amendments or a counter proposal if there was a different approach they preferred.

Note: House Republicans passed a budget on April 15th but, despite the legal requirement to do so, Senate Democrats have not adopted passed a budget in 807 days.  Both chambers must adopt a conference budget in order for it to be statutorily binding.

300.title: GOP Senators Object: No Spending Bills Without A Budget
300.description:
According to the Congressional Budget Act, Congress may not appropriate money for any fiscal year without first passing a budget, which serves as a concrete plan for spending, borrowing, and taxing. Despite this prohibition, Senate Democrats—who have refused to pass a budget for 807 days or make one public at all this year—attempted to move a spending bill on the floor yesterday. In response, Budget Committee Ranking Member Jeff Sessions led his Republican colleagues in a period of extended debate, calling for Congress to fulfill its legal duty to present and adopt a budget (by April 15th of each year).

Sessions raised a point of order [303(c)], which initiated the debate and a vote on whether to uphold or override the legal requirement from the Congressional Budget Act of 1974.

In a landmark vote, Sessions' point of order was supported by 40 Republican Senators to prevent consideration of the appropriations measure (4 GOP Senators were not present to vote), which is particularly noteworthy given that the underlying bill had broad bipartisan support. Under current law, Sessions' point of order requires a majority of Senators to be sustained, so it fell short, but Sessions is also pushing forward a measure to raise the threshold to 60 votes in order to violate the Budget Act requirement.

The Republican Senators in this video, in order of appearance, are Sen. Sessions, Sen. Bob Corker, Sen. John Thune, Sen. Marco Rubio, Sen. Mike Lee, Sen. Rand Paul, Sen. John Cornyn, Sen. Pat Toomey, Sen. Ron Johnson, and Sen. John Barrasso.

301.description:

306.title: "Only The Beginning": Sessions Vows To Fight For Honest, Lawful Budget Process
306.description:
JULY 14, WASHINGTON--Sen. Sessions delivered the following closing statement today in opposition to the consideration of an appropriations bill at a time when Congress has not a passed a budget. The Congressional Budget Act, which contains various enforcement provisions to help Congress ensure honest accounting, contains a "point of order" that prohibits consideration of any appropriations bills in such cases.

A budget serves as a guide for the nation's overall levels of spending, borrowing, and taxing, and Congress is required by law to adopt a budget each year. Despite this legal requirement, it has now been 806 days since the Democrat-controlled Senate has passed a budget, leading to Sessions raising the point of order against the pending appropriations bill.

Sessions also announced he would continue to looking for opportunities to strengthen the point of order by offering an amendment to increase the vote threshold to 60 Senators.

307.title: Sessions Leads Floor Debate: No Spending Bills Without A Budget
307.description:
Senator Jeff Sessions called for an extended GOP floor debate as the Senate prepared to consider the first appropriations bill of the year -- even though the Democrat-led has shirked its legal duty to pass a budget for more than 800 straight days.

Budget Committee Ranking Member Jeff Sessions raised a point of order [303 (c)] which initiated the debate and a vote on whether to uphold or override the legal requirement from the Congressional Budget Act of 1974.

In a landmark vote, Sessions' point of order was supported by 40 Republican Senators to prevent consideration of the appropriations measure (4 GOP Senators were not present to vote), which is particularly noteworthy given that the underlying bill had broad bipartisan support. Under current law, Sessions' point of order requires a majority of Senators to be sustained, so it fell short, however Sessions is pushing forward a measure to raise the threshold to 60 votes in order to violate the Budget Act requirement.

312.title: FULL SPEECH - No Spending Bills Without A Budget, Sessions Warns Dems
312.description:
JULY 13, WASHINGTON--Sen. Sessions announced on the Senate floor this morning that he would be using a provision in the Congressional Budget Act, known as a point of order, in an effort to prevent Congress from appropriating money when it hasn't passed a budget. Sessions also announced that he would be introducing an amendment to strengthen the point of order by requiring a higher vote threshold before it could be waived.

313.title: No Spending Bills Without A Budget, Sessions Warns Dem Majority
313.description:
