314.title: Republicans United On Need To Change Spending And Debt Trajectory
314.description:
JULY 12, WASHINGTON--Sen. Sessions hosted a colloquy today on the Senate Floor with Sens. Ron Johnson, Mike Lee, and Roger Wicker to address the need for a Balanced Budget Amendment, and the need for Senate Democrats to present a serious, concrete budget plan that can be reviewed by Congress and the American people.

As Sen. Wicker stated, "the president's budget was a nonstarter. I think that if the Senate Democratic version ever were to be devised and brought to the floor, it would be a nonstarter, which is why we haven't seen a proposal in over 800 days." All four Senators urged openness in the debt ceiling negotiations, noting the talks have taken place behind closed doors.

315.title: "Forgive Me If I'm Not Impressed" With Democrats' Phantom Budget, Sessions Declares
315.description: JULY 12, WASHINGTON--Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor last night to respond to Budget Committee Chairman Kent Conrad's discussion of the still-unseen Senate Democrat budget plan—803 days since the Democrat-led Senate has adopted a budget. Although selective details have been leaked to the Washington Post, Sessions noted that Democrats still refuse to release any concrete plan that can be analyzed by the Congressional Budget Committee or the American public, as required by law.

316.title: Democrats Resist Responsible Cuts To Massive Gov't
316.description: This morning on FOX's America's Newsroom, Sen. Sessions explained that the $2 trillion dollar in cuts Democrat were apparently willing to accept fell far short of those cuts contained in Republican budget proposals, and represent less than a 5% reduction in federal spending over the next 10 years—during which time we are projected to spend $46 trillion, growing the debt by a total of $13 trillion.

317.title: On "Face The Nation," Sessions Says No Bailout For Big Spenders In Washington
317.description:
JULY 10, WASHINGTON--As the August 2nd deadline approaches for a debt-limit increase, Sen. Sessions appeared on CBS News' "Face the Nation" this morning to discuss the status of the negotiations. Sessions pushed back on the claim that taxes need to be increased as part of any deal, pointing to the fact that non-defense discretionary spending has surged 24 percent in the last two years. He also dispelled the notion that the Bush tax cuts contributed to our deficits: revenue went up every year after those tax cuts were enacted, and only recently have declined because of the poor economy.

On that note, Sessions blamed the grim jobs report last week on our unsustainably high level of debt. The U.S. currently has a debt-to-GDP ratio well above the threshold identified by economists as harmful to economic growth and job creation.

Finally, Sessions raised concerns about the as-yet-unseen Senate Democrat budget plan, which is estimated (based on news reports) to have a tax hike to spending cut ratio of almost 2-to-1.

318.title: Day 800: Sessions On Grim Jobs Report, Debt Ceiling Negotiations
318.description:
On the 800th day the nation has gone without a budget because Senate Democrats refused to pass one, Sen. Sessions appeared on FOX News' "Happening Now" to respond to the June jobs report, which saw the unemployment rate tick up to 9.2%. Sessions pointed out that according to the research of economists Rogoff and Reinhart, the nation's unsustainable debt could already be costing as many as one million jobs per year. Sessions also pushed back against calls for more "stimulus" spending, noting that the last stimulus failed to keep unemployment in check as it was supposed to.

To view the joint statement from Sessions and House Budget Committee Chairman Paul Ryan on the jobs report, please click here: http://goo.gl/x8LnR

319.title: "We Don't Have The Money": Sessions Backs Plan For True Fiscal Discipline
319.description: JULY 7, WASHINGTON--In a press conference today, Sen. Sessions showed his support for the Cut, Cap, and Balance Act sponsored by Sen. Mike Lee, who stated the proposal "forces Washington to balance its books with strict, enforceable fiscal restraints and will cut spending significantly and immediately to improve our economy and create jobs." Sessions urged Washington to follow the lead of American families, businesses, and states and get its spending under control.

320.title: Day 799: GOP Senators On Missing Budget, Need For Openness In Debt Work
320.description: JULY 7, WASHINGTON--Senators Roy Blunt and Ron Johnson joined Sen. Sessions on the floor today to speak about the Senate's schedule this week, the debt ceiling, and the refusal of Senate Democrats to pass a budget in 799 days. Johnson stated that the secret talks are not likely to produce a serious enough budget to confront our country's fiscal challenges, calling instead for the Senate to go through the committee process as required by law. Blunt agreed, noting that Senate Democrats are content to allow legal deadlines to pass without any action.

321.title: President's Budget Plan Fails To Confront Reality, Sessions Says
321.description: JULY 6, WASHINGTON--In a speech on the Senate floor today, Sen. Sessions pushed back against President Obama's claim that "to truly solve our deficit problem... we need to take on spending in domestic programs, in defense programs, [and] in entitlement programs..." In the only formal budget the president has submitted, many departments receive double-digit funding increases. (President Obama has repeatedly asserted that his April speech on deficit reduction amounts to a concrete plan, but as the CBO director recently said, "We don't estimate speeches.")

322.title: Sessions, GOP Colleagues Force Withdrawal Of Libya Resolution, Pressure Dems To Confront Budget
322.description:
JULY 5, WASHINGTON--In a press conference today, Sessions laid out his concerns about the Senate's failure to address any meaningful budget or debt work during the cancelled July 4th recess. Instead, Majority Leader Harry Reid only scheduled votes on a resolution pertaining to Libya and a nonbinding "Sense of the Senate" resolution.

Sessions also pointed out that Democrats have failed to pass a budget for the nation in over 790 days, stating that Democrats are "still unwilling to lay out the kind of numbers it takes to change" our debt trajectory.

323.title: Democrats Relent, Cancel Recess... But Duck Budget Work Anyway
323.description: JULY 5, WASHINGTON--Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid last week cancelled the Senate's 4th of July recess--citing "work to do--but promptly scheduled action on a measure not related to the budget, spending, or debt limit. In response, Sen. Sessions took to the Senate floor today to call for Democrats to refocus their priorities on what has been called the greatest threat to our national security, the debt.

324.title: Sessions Charges: Recess Cancelled For Budget Work, Not Unrelated Libya Resolution
324.description:
JULY 5, WASHINGTON--Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today to announce his opposition to moving to a Libya resolution as long as the Senate has not done any meaningful work to address the budget or looming debt-limit deadline. Sessions noted that the Libya resolution may be an important issue, but "that's not what we need to be doing this week." Sessions also pointed out that President Obama has not even asked for a resolution to authorize the use of force in Libya.

Republican Senators last week opposed going on vacation until the chamber's budget work was completed, prompting Majority Leader Reid to relent and cancel recess. However, Reid failed to schedule any serious work on either the budget or the debt limit -- now 797 days since Senate Democrats last passed a budget.  (To view a letter from Republican Senators objecting to the Memorial Day vacation, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/mIhqNB. To view Sessions' statement announcing opposition to the July 4 recess, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/pHrbIw.)

325.title: Day 797: Johnson Discusses Why GOP Cancelled Dem Recess, Argues for Balanced Budget Amendment
325.description: JULY 5, WASHINGTON--This morning on Fox and Friends, Sen. Ron Johnson discussed this week's cancelled recess and pointed out that Republicans -- not President Obama -- led the charge for the Senate Democrat majority to rescind their planned vacation four weeks prior to the debt ceiling deadline. Johnson also stressed the need for a balanced budget amendment that allows the American people to place firm control over Washington's reckless spending.

326.title: Portman: "It's Not Time To Raise Taxes"
326.description: JULY 5, WASHINGTON--While recent news reports have suggested that Democrats may be open to spending cuts in exchange for tax increases as part of a debt-limit deal, Sen. Rob Portman spoke on FOX today to push back, saying that tax increases would be detrimental to our fragile economic recovery.

327.title: Sessions: 7 Days To Review A Debt Deal
327.description:
JULY 3, WASHINGTON--Sessions appeared on FOX's America's News HQ this afternoon to push for action to take place on the budget and the debt ceiling. He discussed his proposal to require seven days for the Senate and the American people to review the budget. Sessions had pushed for the recess to be cancelled to work on these matters, but the Senate Democrat majority is still preventing such work from taking place.

Sessions noted, "We should have been working on this all year. We have gone 795 days without a budget. This is one reason why spending is so out of control. The American people did not send us here to permanently increase the size of government."

328.title: Barnes Discusses Sessions' Efforts On Forcing Senate To Confront Budget Work
328.description: JUNE 30, WASHINGTON--On "Special Report with Bret Baier" tonight, the panel discussed the Senate's cancellation of next week's recess, including Sen. Sessions' role in bringing that about.

329.title: Dem Majority Relents, Cancels Recess - But Still Won't Schedule Budget Work
329.description: JUNE 30, WASHINGTON—Sen. Sessions participated in a colloquy with his colleagues today to continue the call for the Senate to finally work on a budget resolution, yet Majority Leader Reid appears poised to have the Senate work next week on matters unrelated to spending and debt. As Sessions noted, Reid has not "provided any impetus to produce a budget" in over 790 days now.

330.title: GOP Senators Tell Dem Leaders: Allow Budget Work Next Week - FULL VERSION
330.description:
JUNE 30, WASHINGTON--In a lengthy colloquy on the Senate floor today, several Republican Senators called on the Democrat leadership not to waste the Senate's time with trivial matters next week.

Majority Leader Reid announced today he was heeding the Republicans' call to cancel the upper chamber's July 4th recess since no budget work had been done, but it currently remains to be seen if the Majority Leader will attempt to bring up any budget or spending bills. Indeed, in a unanimous consent request today, Majority Leader Reid asked that the chamber take up a resolution dealing with the conflict in Libya.

Republicans, on the other hand, have been insisting that the Senate focus on a budget. As of today, it has been 792 days since the Democrat-led Senate has passed a budget resolution, and they have not introduced one at all this year.

331.title: Sessions To Reid, Senate Dems: Will You Allow Real Work On Budget During Cancelled Recess?
331.description:
JUNE 30, WASHINGTON--On the Senate floor today, Majority Leader Harry Reid confirmed that the Senate would be staying in session next week because of unspecified "work to do." 

Sen. Sessions responded, challenging the Majority Leader to bring up budget proposals that will actually change the debt trajectory we're on: "I'm not at all sure that the plan is to deal with anything involving the greatest threat to our nation, which is our debt. Apparently they want to talk about other issues... We ought to have a proposal brought forth so it can be amended, so it can be analyzed... that's why we need to be here next week, not to deal with a patent bill or some other legislation."

332.title: FOX: Sessions And GOP Called On Senate To Cancel Vacation Long Before Obama Weighed In
332.description:
JUNE 30, WASHINGTON--On "FOX and Friends" this morning, the anchors noted that President Obama has been largely absent from the deficit reduction debate up to this point.

While the president yesterday called on Congress to remain in town next week to work on budget issues, Sen. Sessions and his Republican colleagues had been pushing for that for over a month. (See the letter, dated May 26, in which the Senators ask Majority Leader Reid to cancel any vacation unless and until the Democrat Majority brings forward a budget plan: http://1.usa.gov/mIhqNB)

333.title: On Lou Dobbs, Sessions Urges Obama To Reveal Details From Secret Budget Talks
333.description: "This Senate Democratic leadership wanted to go home for recess, but I think they are very uneasy about it because the American people are very worried about the debt... Our economy is at risk. We need to take firm, clear action."

334.title: CNN's E.D. Hill Interviews Sessions on Push for Transparency in Debt Negotiations
334.description:
JUNE 29, WASHINGTON--Sen. Sessions joined E.D. Hill on CNN to dicuss the debt talks and the need cut wasteful Washington spending, which he pointed out has increased by 24 percent under President Obama.

Sessions also urged for the ongoing secret debt ceiling negotiations to be made public well in advance of the August 2nd deadline: "An agreement to put us on a sound economic course is very, very important. It should be reached well before August 2nd, and my biggest concern is that the president continues to meet with just a few people, as his vice president has, and they've proposed nothing. And week after week, month after month have gone by."

335.title: Broke or Balanced: Sessions And United GOP Push For Balanced Budget Amendment
335.description: JUNE 29, WASHINGTON—Sen. Sessions joined his GOP colleagues at a press conference this morning to renew the push for Balanced Budget Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, which is sponsored by every Senate Republican. With the President calling for "balance" through higher taxes, Senate Republicans are unified behind an actual balanced budget.

336.title: Sessions Leads Call For Senate Dems To Cancel Recess For Work On Debt Ceiling, Budget
336.description:
While Democrats who control the Senate's schedule have been planning to go on vacation next week, Sen. Sessions has been urging that the chamber remain in session to begin work on a budget plan and a debt ceiling package. He spoke on the Senate floor today to reiterate his call for Majority Leader Reid to hold a vote to go on vacation. (Last month, Sessions sent a letter, signed by 46 Republicans, urging the Senate to remain in town to carry out its fundamental obligation of passing a budget plan.)

Sessions said that "we owe the people we serve an open, honest debate over the debt limit," but pointed out that this cannot occur if the Senate adjourns for a week.

337.title: Pressing For Transparency, Sessions Rejects Tax Hikes To Fund Wasteful Spending
337.description:
On Bloomberg TV this morning, Sen. Sessions called on the president to display leadership and finally explain to the American people the truth about the looming debt crisis. In response to the recent developments in Greece, Sessions noted that "Greece is not off the radar screen" as Senate Democrats continue to refuse to bring a budget up for public review.

It has now been 791 days since the Democrat-led Senate has passed a budget, and they have neglected to bring forward a plan at all this year. Meanwhile, negotiations continue at the White House in secret over a deal to increase the federal government's borrowing limit.

338.title: Thune: Let's Have A Public Budget Debate
338.description: On America's Newsroom this morning, Senator John Thune agreed with the growing consensus that "budget talks need to take place in the public arena." Thune noted that due to Senate Democrats' refusal to bring a budget to the floor, Congress has operated without a budget for 790 days now. Thune also called for a Balanced Budget Amendment to impose discipline to rein in wasteful Washington spending.

339.title: Bill Kristol Encourages Budget Negotiations To Be Opened To Public
339.description: On the "Special Report" roundtable tonight, panelists agreed that secret budget negotiations need to be brought before the public for review and analysis. As Weekly Standard editor Bill Kristol said, "This is kind of important. We do have a tradition in this country that things are debated in Congress and in the media, and if legislation is going to be proposed, there are committee hearings... it's all [being done] behind closed doors. I really think it's bizarre."

340.title: Portman and Thune: We Can't Spend Our Way Out Of Debt
340.description: In a colloquy on the Senate floor, Senator Portman joined Senator Thune to call for spending restraint rather than tax increases in any effort to reduce our deficits. The Senators also discussed academic research that conclusively shows that high levels of debt and deficits undermine confidence, harm economic growth, and prevent job creation.

341.title: Sessions Urges President To Reveal White House Tax Plan From Secret Meetings
341.description:
In an interview on FOX News today, Sen. Sessions said that the breakdown of the Biden debt talks should bring secret, closed-door negotiations to a close and commence a more open, public process. He also called on Democrats to reveal the tax plan they had been pushing behind closed doors: "if they're so proud of their plan, let's see what kind of taxes they were proposing."

Sessions also called on President Obama to finally show the leadership that he has thus far failed to demonstrate. (The president's original budget, which he apparently abandoned in favor of a later speech on deficit reduction, was voted down 0-97. And the Director of the Congressional Budget Office recently said that the president's deficit speech lacked any sort of detail that would be required from a formal plan.)

342.title: Sessions: Time For Secret Debt Talks To See Light of Day
342.description:
Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor this evening to reiterate his call for secret, closed-door negotiations on the debt limit to be made public and to move to an open process before the American people. Earlier today, House Majority Leader Eric Cantor and Senate Minority Whip Jon Jyl announced that they were suspending their participation in the deficit reduction talks led by Vice President Biden because of Democrat demands for tax hikes.

Sessions also urged President Obama to heed the warnings from economists and the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office that failing to cut spending, or an insistence on raising taxes, will further harm the economy: "Raising taxes to pay for excess spending is a refusal to recognize that there are limits to how much we can spend and how much we can tax."

343.title: FOX On Sessions' Call For Openness In Debt Negotiations
343.description:
Earlier today, House Majority Leader Eric Cantor and Senate Minority Whip Jon Kyl suspended their participation in the White House-led negotiations over raising the debt ceiling in light of a continuing push from Democrat leaders to increase taxes as part of any deal to increase the borrowing limit. Sessions renewed his call for a more open process where the public and Congress have an opportunity to study and scrutinize any plan. To read Sessions' statement, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/jBFQyI.

Shannon Bream raised the Sessions' concerns during a segment on the day's developments with Congressman James Lankford.

344.title: CBO Long-Term Outlook Understates Danger, FOX Reports
344.description:
A new report from the Congressional Budget Office today revealed that the U.S.' mounting debt threatens the economy in the near term and risks a full-scale crisis in the long term. As FOX Business economic analyst Stuart Varney said, "Our debt is now bigger than China's entire economy... [we are] clearly getting to the point where people who you want to lend you money will say 'We're not going to lend you any more money, you're borrowing too much...'"

While the CBO's projections are troubling enough, the office itself acknowledges that it understates the risks because high levels of debt threaten the economy with a Greece-style crisis. In the face of urgent calls for action, Senate Democrats have still yet to produce a budget this year or pass one in 784 days.

345.title: Former Obama Spokesman Says U.S. "Doing Okay" With No Budget
345.description:
Ranking Member Jeff Sessions has, for the past several weeks, been pressuring Senate Democrats for failing to produce a budget despite being required by law to do so each year. It has now been 782 days since the Democrat-led upper chamber has passed a budget, and they have failed to even produce a plan this year.

In the 782 days since the Senate passed a budget, the nation has spent $7.1 trillion--including almost $500 billion in interest payments--and racked up $3.2 trillion in gross federal debt. Meanwhile, more than 22 million Americans remain unemployed or underemployed (although around 90,000 federal workers have been hired over that period).

Despite these troubling figures, former Obama spokesman Bill Burton said on FOX News Sunday yesterday that "the country's still running. Like, we're doing okay without a budget in the sense that nothing's shutting down."

346.title: Enzi: 777 Days With No Budget "Not How We Ought To Be Operating"

347.title: Thune: 777 Days Without Addressing Most Predictable Economic Crisis In Nation's History
347.description: Senator Thune pointed out today three important numbers that the American people need to focus on to help understand the dimension of our nation's debt problem.

348.title: Sessions Responds To Reid's Challenge; Budget Issues "Not Important"?
348.description:
On the Senate floor this morning, Majority Leader Harry Reid said: "I heard our friend, the Ranking Member on the Budget Committee, come here and talk for hours, and he keeps talking about things that really have no bearing on what I think is important for the country today..."

Sessions' recent floor speeches, viewable on this YouTube channel, have focused on controlling spending and debt, creating needed jobs through economic growth, and the fact that Senate Democrats have not passed a budget in 776 days--or even offered one this year--despite being required to do so by law.

Sessions spoke on the Senate floor this afternoon to respond to the Majority Leader's assertions and to argue that budget, spending, and economic issues should be the highest priority for the Senate right now, particularly at a time of 9.1 percent unemployment and approximately $5 trillion in new gross federal debt that will have accumulated since the President took office until the end of this year.

Sessions also referenced a letter he and House Budget Committee Chairman Paul Ryan sent to President Obama today concerning Medicare. That letter may be viewed here (http://1.usa.gov/jbWDHH), and a statement from Sessions about it may be viewed here (http://1.usa.gov/k3Ns9G).

349.title: Sessions Says To Democrat Leaders: Let's See The Secret Budget
349.description:
It's been 775 days since Senate Democrats passed a budget and they have not even presented at a plan at all this year. Instead, they held numerous closed-door meeting—weeks past the legal deadline for budget work—but never once making a budget plan public. House Republicans, on the other hand, passed a budget by the statutory deadline.

Meanwhile, with the debt limit nearing, the White House has organized a series of close-door meeting to hammer out a solution, but has also failed to make any plan public. Sessions expressed his concerns about disengaging the public and disregarding the budget process: "I think it's time for these meetings to start getting over with. I think it's time for us to start seeing some numbers... This is how you do business in a democracy, last I heard."

350.title: Senator Ron Johnson: We Are Looking At The Bankrupting of America
350.description: Senator Ron Johnson appeared on FOX News' America's Newsroom this morning to address the ongoing budget battle and to call the President into action on the debt ceiling.

351.title: Day 771: With No Senate Budget, Thune Calls For Meaningful Action On Spending, Debt
351.description: Senator Thune challenged the Senate Democrats to create a honest budget that will restore economic confidence and confront our rising debt.

352.title: Sessions Debates CNN Host Over Economic Philosophy, Jobs, Debt
352.description:
On CNN this morning, Sen. Sessions addressed the debt ceiling negotiations, the Biden talks, and Democrats' unwillingness to produce a budget.  It has been 771 days since the Democrat-led Senate has passed a budget and one has not even been offered this year.  During this debt the debt has swelled by another $3.2 trillion.

While host Christine Romans suggested that more deficit spending is needed to stimulate the economy, Sessions pushed back, noting that two and a half years of borrowing and spending have failed to produce the desired results, instead leaving the country with massive new debt and 9.1 percent unemployment. But despite these troubling statistics, Democrat-led Senate continues to stonewall the adoption of a much-needed budget -- thus further undermining economic certainty and confidence.

353.title: McConnell: Senate Democrats Are Hindering Our Economy
353.description: On the Senate floor earlier this morning, Minority Leader Mitch McConnell noted the absence of a budget and lack of effort to produce one by the Senate Democrats.  He asked, "If the White House doesn't have a plan to pay down the debt or preserve entitlements, why should people have any confidence that something will be done?"

354.title: To Put America Back To Work, The Senate Needs To Go Back To Work
354.description:
Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today to lay out the dangers that America's growing debt burden is already placing on the economy. As reported in the study by the economists Reinhart and Rogoff--a study that was endorsed by Treasury Secretary Geithner and the chairman of Morgan-Stanley--countries with high debt-to-GDP ratios are consigned to slower economic growth than countries with manageable debt. The U.S.' debt, currently at 95 percent of GDP, is already past the warning threshold identified by Reinhart and Rogoff.

Based on estimates from President Obama's Council of Economic Advisors, this means we could be putting as many as one million jobs per year at risk.

Despite these threats, it has now been 770 days since the Democrat Senate has passed a budget. As Sessions noted, "the failure of this body to produce a spending plan to tackle our nation's debt only creates more uncertainty in the economy. Doubt and fear are driving away jobs, stifling growth and investments. That is a fact."

To read Sessions' full remarks, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/m9HIof

355.title: Day 770: Thune On MSNBC to Discuss Economy, Lack Of Senate Democrat Budget
355.description:
In an interview on MSNBC this morning, Sen. John Thune pushed back on calls to raise taxes, saying that "what we have here is a spending problem, not a revenue problem." Reports suggest that the talks led by Vice President Biden may result in tax increases as part of any effort to reduce the deficit.

Thune also noted the lack of a Senate budget for 770 days, and called on the Obama Administration to pursue economic policies to bring down unemployment and gas prices, rather than drive them up.

356.title: Day 768: Prosperity or Decline, Sessions Explains Need for Budget That Fuels Economy
356.description:
In an interview last night on FOX Business, Sen. Sessions pointed to the recent unemployment figures as evidence that the Democrat-led Senate is failing to do its duty by preventing Congress from adopting a budget.  Senate Democrats have not presented a budget plan at all this year or passed one in 768 days.

During the interview, Sessions stressed that our rapidly accumulating debt was leading us to economic decline and that we needed a budget that would change course and lead us to prosperity.

He also raised questions about the closed-door budget negotiations being conducted by Vice President Biden: "Do the American people know who's in those meetings? What are they saying? What plans are they going to plop down for us and ask us to sign with some short notice in the Congress? I don't think that's the right way. We should be doing it openly, through the [Budget] Committee."

357.title: As Americans Lose Their Jobs, Senate Dems Won't Perform Their Own
357.description:
In a speech on the Senate floor last night, Sen. Sessions noted a string of recent bad economic indicators, and took the Democrat Senate to task for failing to produce a budget. As of June 6, it had been 768 days since the Democrat-controlled Senate had passed a budget, and the majority party has yet to even schedule a Budget Committee meeting to begin work on a proposal this year (http://1.usa.gov/ksIO0s).

Sessions suggested that the problem stems from the Democrats' inability to put forward their economic vision in a form the American people would support: "When you produce a budget, you have to set forth for the entire world--the financial world, the American people, the political world, the individual citizens of this Republic--what your plans are for the future... this Keynesian, "spend, tax, spend" idea of how to make an economy grow is not sound. We've tried it... You can't borrow your way out of debt."

358.title: Sessions Chides Senate Dem Leaders For Ducking Recess Vote, Dodging Budget Work
358.description: Prior to the adjournment for a week of "pro forma" sessions, Sen. Sessions spoke last week about the Senate Democrats' failure to pass a budget, failure to bring a budget up to be worked on in Committee, and their use of a procedural loophole to take a weeklong vacation without having to vote on it.

359.title: Day 762: Senate Democrats Respond To Growing Calls For Action On Budget
359.description:
Yesterday - 762 days since last passing a budget -- the Democrat-led Senate convened for a "pro forma" session in which the chamber was gaveled in and then gaveled out without conducting any legislative business or taking any action to craft a budget plan to address our dangerously rising debt.

Sen. Sessions and his Republican colleagues last week called on the Senate to remain in session to work on solutions to the nation's fiscal challenges (http://1.usa.gov/j7cHgN), but Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid instead opted for a series of pro forma sessions to prevent the chamber from doing any actual work. [Note: The pro forma decision also allowed Senate Democrats to avoid having to vote for a one-week vacation for themselves.]

360.title: Full Speech: No Budget? No Vacation. Sessions Challenges Senate Democrats
360.description:
Sen. Sessions challenged Senate Democrats for failing to pass a budget in 754 days, and failing to introduce a budget plan at all this year--pointing out that Senate Dems have even blocked the Committee from meeting to work on a budget even though they acknowledge having some form of a plan that they are unwilling to make public.

Sessions announced that he would object to any unanimous consent request to allow the Senate to recess for the Memorial Day break if Senate Democrats continue to shut down the budget process.  He also argued that Senate Dems have an obligation as leaders--and in keeping with Congressional statute--to present an alternate vision to the House GOP plan if they wish to continue their attempts to savage it.  Later in the week, on Thursday, Sessions sent a letter to Maj. Leader Reid, signed by his Senate Republican colleagues, joining together to urge him not to adjourn the chamber for recess until the statutory budget process was allowed to move forward.

Highlighting the extraordinary cynicism of Majority Leader Reid's effort to bring up for a vote and to defeat GOP Budget while offering no Dem Budget (with Reid saying it would be 'foolish' to do so), Sessions said he looked forward to voting for the House GOP plan (which any member can bring up at any time under Budget Act rules) but would not consent to any unanimous consent deal that supports Reid's planned theater.

361.title: Sessions: It Would Be "Foolish" Not To Pass A Budget As The Law Requires
361.description: On FOX News this morning, Sen. Sessions described it as "utterly irresponsible" for Senate Democrats to plan a series of show votes--all intended to fail--on competing budget proposals without producing their own plan. As required by the Congressional Budget Act, each House of Congress must pass a budget by April 15, but it has now been 756 days since the Senate has passed a budget.

362.title: Show Us The Budget: McConnell Floor Remarks On Senate Dem Intransigence
362.description: On the Senate floor today, Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell accused Democrat leaders of playing politics with our nation's budget and debt crisis: "After producing no budget [for 755 days], after offering no plan, and with no plan in sight... evidently Democrats have decided that avoiding this crisis helps them in the next election.

363.title: Ayotte On FOX Talks GOP Letter To Reid Over Missing Dem Budget
363.description: The newest member of the Senate Budget Committee, Sen. Kelly Ayotte, appeared on America's Newsroom today to discuss the Senate Republicans' letter to Majority Leader Harry Reid asking for action from Senate Democrats on the budget. All 47 Senate Republicans signed onto the letter and noted that although the Senate has a statutory obligation to pass a budget each year, it's been over 750 days since the Democrat-led Senate has done so. (Majority Leader Reid recently said in an interview that it would be "foolish" for Democrats to reveal their budget to the public at this time.)

364.title: No Budget? No Vacation. Sessions Challenges Senate D's on Refusal To Publicly Present Their Plan
364.description:
In a searing speech on the Senate Floor today, Sen. Sessions challenged Senate Democrats for failing to pass a budget in 754 days, and failing to introduce a budget plan at all this year--pointing out that Senate Dems have even blocked the Committee from meeting to work on a budget even though they acknowledge having some form of a plan that they are unwilling to make public.

Sessions announced that he would object to any unanimous consent request to allow the Senate to recess for the Memorial Day break if Senate Democrats continue to shut down the budget process.  He also argued that Senate Dems have an obligation as leaders--and in keeping with Congressional statute--to present an alternate vision to the House GOP plan if they wish to continue their attempts to savage it.  Highlighting the extraordinary cynicism of Majority Leader Reid's effort to bring up for a vote and to defeat GOP Budget while offering no Dem Budget (with Reid saying it would be 'foolish' to do so), Sessions said he looked forward to voting for the House GOP plan (which any member can bring up at any time under Budget Act rules) but would not consent to any unanimous consent deal that supports Reid's planned theater.

Click here (http://1.usa.gov/mtQQPh) for a full copy of the Senator's speech.

[Also, from earlier today, to view a copy of a letter signed by all 47 GOP Senators to Reid click here: http://1.usa.gov/iIIniQ]

365.title: Top Budget And Finance Republicans Engage In Colloquy On Senate Floor To Call For Budget
365.description: Sen. Sessions, Ranking Member of the Budget Committee, and Sen. Hatch, Ranking Member of the Finance Committee, spoke on the Senate floor last week to discuss the need for Senate Democrats to produce a budget. As of today, it has been 754 days since the Senate has passed a budget, and the Democrats who control the Senate have yet to bring forward a plan or even schedule a committee markup this year.

366.title: York: Senate No Closer To Passing Budget Than It Was A Month Ago

367.title: How Many Americans Would Support Dem Senate Skipping The Nation's Budget?
367.description: Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor about the need for the Senate to pass a budget.

368.title: Sessions: Senate Dems Must Produce A Budget
368.description: Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor about the need for the Senate to pass a budget.

369.title: Senate Democrats In 'Disarray' On Budget
369.description: Sen. Sessions appeared on America's Newsroom today to discuss the latest in budget talks and the continuing failure of Senate Dems to produce a budget and present it to the American people.  As of May 11th it's been 742 days since the Democrat-led Senate has passed a budget resolution.

370.title: Real Balance Means Shifting Power From Washington Back To The People
370.description: U.S. Sen. Jeff Sessions (R-AL), Ranking Member of the Senate Budget Committee, made the following comments  as details began to emerge about the composition of the Senate Democrat budget, which has yet to be presented publicly. News reports have indicated that the balance of tax increases to spending cuts is likely to be as heavy as 1-to-1. Sessions previewed a new Budget Committee analysis of available research that shows that countries that turn to spending cuts, rather than tax increases, more effectively reduce their deficits and enjoy better economic growth than countries that rely more heavily on tax increases.

371.title: Sessions and Ryan Talk Budget on Greta
371.description:
In an interview on FOX News last night, Sen. Sessions and House Budget Committee Chairman Paul Ryan discussed the Senate Democrats' delay in presenting a budget to the public and bringing it before the Senate Budget Committee to mark up.

Sessions noted: "The Democratic Senate has failed to act. I think it's because they cannot bring forth a budget that their members support, that the American people will support. And they understand that, they know that, and they've got a big problem."

372.title: Where Is The Democrat Budget?
372.description:
Speaking on the Senate floor today, Sen. Sessions pointed out that it has been 741 days since Senate Democrats have passed a budget. Despite the statutory requirement to pass a budget by April 15, Senate Democrats have yet to bring forward a plan or schedule a hearing to mark one up. A mark-up was originally slated for Monday, May 9, then postponed until Tuesday, then postponed until Wednesday, and now has been put off indefinitely.

(Note: the Republican-led House passed its budget on April 15. To view a letter from all Budget Committee Republicans asking Chairman Conrad to schedule a mark-up and present his plan to the public, please click here http://1.usa.gov/kYIJvx. To see the Budget Committee's analysis of President Obama's deficit speech 'framework,' please click here http://1.usa.gov/ilIK7V .)

373.title: Sessions Wary Of Secret Meetings, Tax Increases As Solution To Debt Problem
373.description:
In an interview on MSNBC's "The Daily Rundown" today, Sen. Sessions spoke out against tax increases as a solution to solving our nation's fiscal challenges: "[Neither] the American people, nor I, will support a tax increase until we've seen that Congress is willing to restrain its spending. That is a fact."

Sessions also expressed concern about the prospect of another secret, closed-door meeting on debt reduction. As Sessions noted in a statement yesterday, "No amount of closed-door meetings, commissions, or summits will change the basic fact that in order to move forward the White House and the Democrat Senate must put forward an honest plan that ends the Washington spending spree instead of raising taxes to pay for it."

374.title: More Closed-Door Meetings Not The Answer For Dealing With Debt, Sessions Says
374.description: Ahead of a planned White House meeting on deficit reduction, Sen. Sessions today expressed reservations about yet another closed-door meeting or summit. Sessions has been calling in recent weeks for Democrats to put forward a serious, credible plan for confronting our record levels of spending and debt. Although the Senate is required by law to pass a budget by April 15, Senate Democrats have yet to come forward with a plan or even schedule a hearing to begin work on a budget resolution.

375.title: YouTube Town Hall: Congress Must Stop Spending Money We Don't Have, Sessions Says
375.description:
Sen. Sessions today called on Congress to make responsible choices today to save our children from even tougher choices tomorrow.

In particular, Sen. Sessions pointed out that the non-defense discretionary budget has surged nearly 25 percent over the past few years, at a time when inflation has only been around 2 percent.

This video was created as part of YouTube Town Hall, answering the question "Can Congress address our surging deficits through discretionary spending cuts alone?" To view the debate and choose your side, please visit http://www.YouTube.com/YTTownHall.

376.title: Debunked: President's 'Framework' To Reduce Deficit $4T Would Actually Grow It By $2.2T
376.description:
The Budget Committee today released an analysis that revealed the president's 'framework' to reduce the deficit by $4 trillion would actually grow it $2.2 trillion beyond the CBO baseline.

To view that analysis, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/ilIK7V

377.title: Sessions Tells Holder On DOJ Budget: Better Management Saves Money
377.description: At a Judiciary Committee hearing today, Sen. Sessions rejected Attorney General Eric Holder's assessment that more money and resources are needed to be able to combat fraud.

378.title: We Need More Than A 'Vision,' Sessions Says--We Need A Plan
378.description: Sen. Sessions was interviewed on CNN's American Morning this morning to lay out what he hopes and expects to hear from President Obama at this afternoon's speech. In particular, Sessions said that any "vision" needs to be presented in concrete, detailed form that can be analyzed by CBO as the law requires.

379.title: Krauthammer Agrees: Obama Needs To Submit New Budget Plan

380.title: Sessions Defends Ryan Budget
380.description: Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today to contrast the unserious budget plan submitted by President Obama with Paul Ryan's "serious, honest, straightforward" House budget resolution.

381.title: Show Us The Numbers: Sessions Asks President To Offer New Budget With Specific Cuts
381.description:
Speaking on the Senate floor today, Sen. Sessions previewed President Obama's planned speech tomorrow on the budget. Sessions said that, if the president's speech is an apparent admission that his previous budget was insufficient, then President Obama and OMB should submit a sufficiently detailed budget that the plan could be analyzed by CBO.

Sessions said that "I hope [tomorrow's speech] does not continue the pattern of retreat that is already emerging, where the president supports deficit reduction in theory but resists it in practice, and [then] claims credit when he's forced to accept reductions."

382.title: Sessions Calls On President To Submit New Budget Plan To Congress
382.description:
In light of an announcement by White House political advisor David Plouffe that President Obama would deliver a speech on deficit reduction, Sen. Sessions today called on the president to submit a new, concrete plan to Congress for addressing our long-term deficits and debt. Sessions pointed out that the president is required by law to submit a budget to Congress and that his existing formal submission dramatically increases both taxes and spending and, according to the Congressional Budget Office, will never produce an annual deficit of less than $748 billion -- eventually doubling our gross national debt.

Related content: http://budget.senate.gov/republican/pressarchive/2011-04-08ByTheNumbers.pdf

383.title: Sessions And Schumer Continue Debate—Spending, Debt Limit, Budget
383.description: After their appearance last week on ABC, Sen. Sessions and Sen. Schumer continued their debate today over the size and role of government and the level of government spending. While Sen. Sessions argued that the Congress must heed the will of the American people and lower overall government spending, Sen. Schumer suggested that tax increases were a better way to shrink the deficit.

384.title: As Shutdown Looms, Sessions Challenges Elitism Of Those Protecting Big Government
384.description: On the Senate floor tonight, Sessions criticized Democrat leaders for their disparaging comments about Americans calling for a change in the way Washington does business.

385.title: Sens. Sessions and Whitehouse Debate Spending Priorities
385.description:
Tonight on the Senate floor, Sen. Sessions debated one of his Democrat colleagues about the merits of using taxpayer dollars to fund Planned Parenthood, the leading abortion provider in the country. Sessions pointed out, however, that the current one-week CR does not include the "riders" that Democrats have oppossed.

Sen. Sessions also defended Tea Party supporters against charges of "extremism" from leading Democrat senators.

386.title: Sessions Scolds Dem Leaders On Shutdown: American People 'Not Going To Buy' Your Arguments
386.description: Sen. Sessions delivered impassioned remarks on the Senate floor today to address the looming possibility of a government shutdown. Sessions strongly rejected the blame and aspersions that Democrats have been casting on Republicans. He pointed out that the Republican-led House has passed both a full-year and a short-term CR, while the Democrat-controlled Senate has passed nothing.

387.title: To Avoid Shutdown, Sessions Issues Call To Senate Dems: Pass The House Bill
387.description:
Sen. Sessions rejected the notion today that Republicans want to shut the government down, pointing out that the Republican-controlled House of Representatives has sent the Senate a bill to fund the government for the rest of the year. The Democrat-led Senate, meanwhile, has not passed that bill or introduced a bill of its own to fund the government.

Sessions said: "I hope we can get things worked out in a way that's consistent with the message of the last election. There was a shellacking of the big spenders... I think it's inevitable that we were going to reduce spending. That was the message of the last election. So to some degree, I think President Obama and the Democrat leadership, particularly in the Senate, were in denial."

388.title: Sessions Applauds House Republican Budget, Reprimands Irresponsibility Of Democrat Leaders
388.description: Sen. Sessions joined members of the House Budget Committee today as they unveiled their FY2012 budget resolution. Sessions congratulated Chairman Ryan and his committee: "The House has stood firm. In the face of all kinds of threats—'We're going to attack you, we're going to use every kind of political force against you'—you have looked the American people in the eye and submitted a fact-based budget that will stand up to scrutiny, that will alter the unacceptable trajectory we're now on... Fundamentally, it's an honest budget."

389.title: Are Experts Who Call On U.S. To Curb Rising Debt 'Extreme' Too?
389.description: Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor yesterday to address Democrat Senate leaders' continued characterizations of Republican efforts to reduce spending as 'extreme.' Sessions pointed to expert testimony that suggests that changing the country's debt trajectory will have a positive influence on jobs and economic growth.

390.title: With No Budget Plan Of Their Own, Dem Senate Leaders Disparage Concerned Americans
390.description:
As House Republicans prepare to release a serious, honest plan to reduce our deficit trajectory, Senate Democrat leaders--who have yet to unveil a budget plan of their own--are now disparaging those concerned Americans who have called for smaller government and less spending.

Speaking on FOX News this morning, Sen. Sessions rejected that approach: "These are good people. They went out in the streets for the first time in their lives. They were afraid for their country, and rightly so... We can't wait. We need to start taking steps [to change our fiscal course] today."

391.title: Sessions Debates Schumer On Spending
391.description:
Today on ABC's "This Week," Sen. Sessions sparred with Sen. Chuck Schumer of New York about the ongoing budget negotiations. While Sen. Schumer stood by his characterization of the Tea Party as "extreme," Sen. Sessions disagreed: "Maybe they don't understand all the realities of Washington politics, but fundamentally, they know this country is on a path to fiscal disaster."

Sessions also urged Congress to pass spending reductions of at least $61 billion to avert the fiscal crisis that Alan Greenspan, Timothy Geithner, and the Fiscal Commission co-chairs have warned about: "The fundamental question is, Are we headed to a financial crisis if we don't get off the fiscal course we're on? We've had witness after witness say that's so.... We've got to take action now."

392.title: All 47 Republican Senators Introduce Balanced Budget Amendment
392.description:
Sen. Sessions joined with Minority Leader Mitch McConnell and other Senate Republicans to introduce a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution. The amendment would require a supermajority vote to raise taxes or increase the debt limit, and also would set a limit on outlays to 18 percent of GDP.

Sen. Sessions' remarks begin at the 10:10 mark.

393.title: Budget Controversy: Sessions Announces Opposition To Nominee With "Stunning" Inexperience
393.description:
Sen. Sessions took to the Senate floor today to lay out his concerns with Heather Higginbottom, President Obama's nominee to be deputy budget director at OMB. While the average nominee for this post has had 6.5 years of budget or finance experience, Ms. Higginbottom has none. (To view the Budget Committee's action alert on the nomination, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/hsqdy3 )

During her confirmation hearing, Ms. Higginbottom attempted to defend false assertions by the president and by budget director Jack Lew concerning the president's budget (http://youtu.be/muXovEBakag ).

394.title: Dem Leaders Think Cutting $61 Billion Out Of $3.7 Trillion Is "Extreme"?
394.description:
On the Senate floor this morning, Sen. Sessions chastened Democrat leaders after it emerged that they were coordinating their talking points to paint Republicans as "extreme." In a conference call yesterday, Sen. Chuck Schumer of New York said, "I always use the word 'extreme'" when discussing Republican plans to reduce spending.

Also yesterday, former DNC Chairman Howard Dean said that "I think it would be the best thing in the world to have a [government] shutdown."

As Sen. Sessions has noted today and in recent days, nearly every freshman Republican lawmaker was elected on promises to reduce spending. The Republican-controlled House of Representatives has already passed a bill to fund the government for the remainder of the fiscal year, but the Democrat-led Senate has not yet done so.

395.title: Republicans Unified On The Need For Meaningful Spending Cuts
395.description:
Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor yesterday to point out that Republicans are unified in their calls for more spending reductions: while 10 Democrats defected from their party's do-nothing plan, every Senate Republican either supported the House plan or called for more cuts.

Sessions also cautioned against a tax-and-spend "compromise": "Endless spending, taxing, and borrowing is a certain path to decline."

396.title: Sessions Speaks In Support Of Latest Spending Reduction, Stresses Need For Further Action
396.description: Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today in support of a continuing resolution to fund the government over the next three weeks while reducing spending by $6 billion. The measure, which passed by a vote of 87--13, follows a resolution early this month to reduce spending by $4 billion over two weeks. Congress must still agree on a continuing resolution for the remainder of the fiscal year.

397.title: Obama Nominee Crumbles Trying To Defend WH Budget Deception
397.description:
The Budget Committee held a hearing today to consider the nomination of Heather Higginbottom to be President Obama's deputy budget director. Sen. Sessions confronted the nominee over false assertions from the White House regarding the president's budget.

Both President Obama and his budget director have repeatedly said that the president's budget allows us to "live within our means," "spend money that we have each year," and "begin paying down our debt." (http://1.usa.gov/hvENzK, http://youtu.be/rTuzmyMwH7E) Numerous fact-check organizations have found these statements to be false, (http://goo.gl/ZuitF) and Sessions has argued that these inaccurate claims undermine efforts to confront our growing fiscal crisis.

In reality, the budget that President Obama submitted adds $13 trillion to the debt, never has a deficit less than $600 billion, and spends more than it takes in every single year. And by the tenth year, interest payments on our debt will rise to $844 billion--more than we spend on Medicare or defense.

Note: Ms. Higginbottom, a former advisor for Obama's presidential campaign, has no formal budget training or experience.

UPDATE 3/18: CBO released its analysis of the president's budget today, finding that the Obama proposal actually conceals $2.3 trillion in deficits. Using more realistic economic assumptions than the White House used, total deficits over the next decade will reach $9.5 trillion. (http://1.usa.gov/fTc9lT)

398.title: Sessions Lists Benefits Of Discretionary Cuts
398.description: Sen. Sessions delivered an opening statement today at a hearing with former Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici and former OMB and CBO Director Alice Rivlin to discuss the report from their bipartisan debt reduction task force. Sessions argued that immediate reductions in discretionary spending will result in numerous benefits, such as spurring economic growth, easing the deficit burden by hundreds of billions of dollars, and helping to avert a debt crisis.

399.title: As Major Investor Gets Rid Of U.S. Bonds, Sessions Urges: Cut Spending Now
399.description:
Warning signs the week point to the urgent need to reduce spending: the world's largest bond fund announced it was eliminating U.S. government debt from its holdings, and in testimony before the Budget Committee, the co-chairs of the president's fiscal commission announced that a debt crisis could be as little as one or two years away.

To view a list of experts' comments about the immediacy of the need to address our debt challenges, please click here: http://1.usa.gov/ejWWoj

400.title: "Token Cuts" Not Acceptable, Sessions Says As CR Fight Rolls On
400.description:
After Senate Democrats blocked a Republican funding plan that would have reduced government spending by a total of $61 billion for the last 7 months of this year--resulting in $862 billion in savings over 10 years (1.65 trillion if the lower levels are sustained for five years)--Sen. Sessions went to the Senate floor to warn that the vote should not be wrongly interpreted as an invitation to negotiate a timid compromise. Sessions pointed out that many of the 11 Democrat senators who opposed the Democrat proposal to cut only $4.7 billion argued that more cuts were needed and that momentum was on the side of taking significant action.

Sessions said that such decisive action now will make our country stronger and more prosperous, and that it will send a clear message to the world that the U.S. is serious about putting its fiscal house in order.

401.title: Prosperity Or Decline, Sessions Lays Out Competing Visions At Deficit Hearing
401.description: Sen. Sessions delivered this opening statement yesterday at the hearing with the co-chairs of President Obama's fiscal commission, Erskine Bowles and Alan Simpson.

402.title: The Appeal: Ahead Of Key Spending Vote, Sessions Makes Case For Action
402.description:
Sen. Sessions spoke on the Senate floor today to draw a clear contrast between the two proposals to fund the government for the remainder of the year: The Republican plan, which cuts $57 billion and would result in significant savings over time if those reductions were held constant, or the Democrat plan, which basically leaves current spending levels unchanged except for a minor $4.6 billion reduction.

UPDATE--The final vote count follows:
• HR 1 (Republican plan): 44-56 
 Yes: 44 R -- 0 D
 No: 3 R -- 52 D -- 1 I
• Dem alternative: 42-58 
 Yes: 0 R -- 42 D
 No: 47 R -- 10 D -- 1 I

403.title: Sessions Discusses House Republican Plan Savings With Fiscal Comm. Co-Chair
403.description: At today's Budget Committee hearing, Sen. Sessions pointed out that the $61 billion in savings from the House Republican plan, if it were built into the CBO baseline, would add up to $862 billion in savings over 10 years, and dramatically more if those cuts are sustained or increased.

404.title: Do Something Or Do Nothing: Sessions Talks Dueling CR's On FOX News
404.description: The Senate is expected to vote today on 2 bills to fund the government for the remainder of this fiscal year: a Republican plan that reduces spending by $61 billion, and a Democrat alternative that reduces just $4.6 billion.

405.title: Spending Showdown: Sessions Criticizes Reid for 'Do-Nothing' Plan
405.description:
House Republicans passed, and the Senate will soon vote on, a spending reduction plan that cuts $61 billion from the budget for the remainder of this year. As a counter-offer, Senate Democrats have proposed a plan that cuts just $4.66 billion from the remainder of this year, and top Democrats have suggested they are not willing to go any further.

Speaking from the Senate floor today after Majority Leader Reid concluded his remarks, Sen. Sessions blasted the Democrats' plan as insufficient, saying, "Those are fake cuts, they're not real cuts. This is Washington talk... Is this what the American people expected when they voted last election and sent a new House of Representatives and new senators here? I don't think so."  

Sessions concluded his remarks by challenging his colleagues: "Our character is tested by how we respond in times of great challenge... Stand and be counted."

If the House Republicans' savings of $61 billion were built into the CBO baseline, savings over 10 years would add up to $862 billion (including interest) and dramatically more if those cuts are either sustained or increased.

406.title: More Spending, More Debt, Fewer Jobs: Sessions On WH Budget
406.description:
After a week of hearings in the Budget Committee, Sen. Sessions took to the Senate floor today to point out the large funding increases being requested by the Obama Administration. Overall, the president's budget would double our national debt--reaching more than $26 trillion by the end of the decade.

The president has repeatedly said that these increases are "investments," but Sessions directly confronts that argument and makes the case for spending reductions that will clear the way for economic growth.

407.title: There They Go Again: Obama Official Repeats Discredited Budget Claim
407.description:
Politifact checked President Obama's statement that the budget "will not add to the debt" and found it false: http://goo.gl/ZuitF

To view the Budget Committee's Republican staff analysis of the budget, which shows that the plan would add $13 trillion to the debt, please click here: http://bit.ly/fpJueP

408.title: Another Obama Official Admits Prez Punted With Budget
408.description:
Speaking today at a hearing to present the Department of Transportation's budget request, Sec. Ray LaHood defended the $435 billion "mystery tax"—a revenue source that is not explained or detailed in the president's budget submission—by saying, "Senator, I think what we need to do is to sit down together and figure this out. And, uh, we're willing to do that."

Sen. Sessions responded, "Well, 'sitting' and 'figuring out' is a little late when you've got a budget that assumes it's going to be done when it's not going to be done."

Last week, Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner admitted that President Obama's budget, even if enacted exactly as submitted to Congress, contains unsustainable obligations.

409.title: Sessions Responds To Passage Of Gov't Funding Bill, Looks Ahead To Future Reductions
409.description:
The Senate today passed, and President Obama signed, a government funding bill that reduces spending by $4 billion from current levels over the next two weeks.

After the vote, Sen. Sessions said in an interview that it was an important first step, but that spending reductions need to be sustained to have a meaningful impact on our deficit.

410.title: Spending Doesn't Equal Investment, Sessions Tells Obama's Energy Secretary
410.description: Sen. Sessions delivered an opening statement today at the hearing to consider the Department of Energy's budget request for Fiscal Year 2012. Sessions stressed to Secretary Steven Chu the need for an energy policy that unlocks America's energy reserves to lower prices and create jobs.

411.title: Sessions To Duncan: 'Why Don't We Just Spend Three Times As Much?'
411.description:
The following exchange occurred as Senator Sessions and Education Secretary Arne Duncan debated how best to confront America's fiscal challenges and to pursue an education strategy that works. Sessions pointed out that dramatic spending increases in recent years have not bridged the international scoring gap, and challenged Secretary Duncan's suggestion that merely spending more money would produce a better result for the country.

Education spending has increased a total of 68 percent over the past three years, including the stimulus. And President Obama's budget calls for an 11-percent increase this year.

The United States currently spends more than $11,500 per student on education, yet ranks 14th in international reading scores. By contrast, New Zealand, Finland, Canada, South Korea, Japan, and Australia all spend less, yet rank higher in international comparisons.

412.title: Sessions: Battle Over The Budget Is Just Beginning
412.description: In this morning's hearing, Sen. Sessions said, "we are going to fight for spending cuts this week, next week, next month, and next year. We are going to fight for spending cuts in the Budget Committee, in the Appropriations Committee, and on the Senate floor. We are going to keep fighting for a leaner, more productive government until we have restored confidence in our economy and put this country back on the right path—the path to prosperity."

413.title: Can't Win Future For Our Children With Borrowed Money, Sessions Tells Education Sec.
413.description: Sen. Sessions delivered this opening statement today at a hearing with Education Secretary Arne Duncan on the Department of Education's FY 2012 budget request. Including the stimulus, education spending over the last three years is 68 percent higher than the previous three, and the president's budget calls for an additional 11 percent increase next year. However, American schools continue to trail in international rankings, meaning that more money is clearly not always the answer.

414.title: Geithner Admits: Obligations In President's Budget 'Unsustainable'
414.description:
Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner today admitted under questioning from Sen. Sessions that the president's own budget, submitted Monday, calls for interest payments and obligations that are "excessively high" and "unsustainable." The president's plan accumulates $13 trillion in new gross debt, with interest payments on the debt rising to $844 billion a year by 2021.

Additionally, the president's budget ignores the recommendations of his own fiscal commission, causing the Democrat Co-Chair of the Commission, Erskin Bowles, to remark that the budget "goes nowhere near where they will have to go to resolve our fiscal nightmare."

297.title: The President's Fiscal Year 2015 Education Budget Request
297.description: Chairman Patty Murray (D-WA) and the Senate Budget Committee held a hearing on the President's Fiscal Year 2015 Education Budget Request with Department of Education Secretary Arne Duncan. At the hearing Murray discussed the education proposals in the President's budget and called on Congress to build on the two-year budget and focus on addressing the education deficit to make sure more Americans have the chance to succeed and contribute to the economy. Murray highlighted the importance of investing in education, from early learning through K-12, to higher education and career training, in order to expand opportunity and make sure the nation stays competitive in the global economy.

298.title: Senate Budget Committee Hearing | 4.8.14 | Chairman Murray Opening Statement
298.description:
Chairman Patty Murray (D-WA) and the Senate Budget Committee held a hearing on Supporting Broad-Based Economic Growth and Fiscal Responsibility through a Fairer Tax Code with majority witnesses John L. Buckley, J.D., former Chief Tax Counsel of the House Committee on Ways and Means, and former Chief of Staff of the Joint Committee on Taxation, and Jane G. Gravelle, Ph.D., Senior Specialist in Economic Policy at the Congressional Research Service. 

At the hearing, Murray discussed policies that would support workers and families by making our tax code fairer, such as the 21st Century Worker Tax Cut Act she recently introduced. Senator Murray also called for closing unfair and inefficient tax loopholes that benefit the wealthiest Americans and biggest corporations, in order to reduce budget deficits and invest in national priorities that support economic growth.

300.title: Senate Budget Committee Hearing | 4.1.14 | Chairman Murray Opening Remarks

At the hearing, Murray addressed the lack of economic mobility and rise of economic inequality, which threatens the middle class -as well as prospects for prosperity and fiscal responsibility. Murray also highlighted ways to expand opportunity to more Americans through supporting workers and struggling families, and addressing deficits in jobs, infrastructure, education, and research, to ensure all Americans have a chance to get ahead.

301.title: SENATOR PATTY MURRAY INTRODUCES THE 21st CENTURY WORKER TAX CUT ACT
301.description: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Patty Murray (D-WA) introduced the 21st Century Worker Tax Cut Act, a bill that would update the tax code to help today's workers and families keep more of what they earn. Complementing critical reforms like raising the minimum wage, the 21st Century Worker Tax Cut Act would update the tax code to provide targeted tax cuts designed for today's workforce.  The bill builds on work incentives both Republicans and Democrats agree have been effective, and it is paid for by closing wasteful and inefficient tax loopholes both parties have proposed eliminating.

302.title: Senate Budget Committee Hearing | 3.12.14 | Chairman Murray Opening Remarks

At the hearing, Murray addressed revenue proposals in the President's budget and discussed ways to encourage job creation and economic growth through the tax code, such as expanding work incentives for struggling Americans and closing wasteful corporate loopholes to invest in rebuilding our transportation infrastructure. Murray also discussed the need to ask the wealthiest Americans and biggest corporations to pay their fair share towards responsibly tackling our long-term budget challenges.

305.description: Chairman Patty Murray (D-WA) and the Senate Budget Committee held a hearing on transitioning from constant crises to broad-based economic growth in 2014. Democratic witnesses included Dr. Mark Zandi, Chief Economist at Moody's Analytics and Robert Greenstein, President of the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities. At the hearing, Murray highlighted that while gridlock and dysfunction have had serious consequences for economic growth in the past few years, the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2013 provides an opportunity for Congress to build on that to transition from lurching from crisis to crisis to working on priorities that help families and communities and drive broad-based economic growth and opportunity.

306.title: Murray Urges Senate to Build on Bipartisan Budget Deal
306.description: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Patty Murray (D-WA) delivered remarks on the Senate floor in support of appropriations legislation that fills in the details of the Bipartisan Budget Act that Murray negotiated with House Budget Committee Chairman Paul Ryan (R-WI) in December. Murray highlighted key investments in families and communities in Washington State and across the country, and called on Congress to pass the legislation and build on it by renewing emergency unemployment benefits and continuing to deliver for the American people through compromise and bipartisanship.

307.title: Chairman Murray Urges Colleagues to Support Bipartisan Budget Act
307.description: On December 17, 2013, Republicans and Democrats in the U.S. Senate voted 67-33 to clear a procedural hurdle and move to a final vote to pass the federal budget agreement Senator Patty Murray (D-WA) reached with Congressman Paul Ryan (R-WI). Democrats and Republicans in the House of Representatives voted overwhelmingly last week to pass the budget agreement.  To become law, the agreement still must pass a final, simple majority vote in the Senate tomorrow.  Once passed, it will only require President Obama's signature to become law. Before the vote, Senator Murray spoke on the Senate floor to urge her colleagues to support the budget agreement.

308.title: Chairman Murray Calls for Compromise to Boost Economy, End Harmful Spending Cuts
308.description: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Patty Murray (D-WA) delivered remarks on the Senate floor outlining her goals for the bipartisan budget conference, including creating jobs, replacing the irresponsible, across-the-board spending cuts, and setting budget levels for at least the short term. In the speech, Murray detailed how budget cuts have had negative consequences in Washington state and across the country. Murray called on members on both sides of the aisle to compromise and find a solution that strengthens the economy, creates jobs, and ends the lurching from crisis to crisis.

309.title: Senate Budget Committee Hearing | 7.23.13 | Chairman Murray Opening Remarks
309.description: Today, Chairman Murray and the Senate Budget Committee held a hearing about the recent encouraging news regarding health care spending trends and delivery system reforms, and discussed areas of further work that focus on aligning incentives and making the system more efficient, rather than simply shifting costs to seniors and families. The cost of health care affects every kitchen table and conference table conversation in the United States, as American households and American businesses face the question of how to pay for the healthcare coverage they want for their families and employees," Chairman Murray said at the hearing.

310.title: Senate Budget Committee Hearing | 7.23.13 | Chairman Murray Opening Remarks
310.description:
Chairman Patty Murray (D-WA) and the Senate Budget Committee held a hearing on the impact defense sequestration is having on our economy and our military preparedness. Majority witnesses included Jennifer-Cari Green, a full-time employee at Madigan Army Medical Center, single mother and college student, who is dealing with being furloughed, Mark Klett, a service-disabled veteran small business owner, and President and CEO of Klett Consulting Group, and Robert Work, Chief Executive Officer of the Center for a New American Security. 

At the hearing, witnesses testified about the impact the irresponsible automatic defense cuts from sequestration are having on our national security, veterans, families, and communities. Chairman Murray highlighted the need to replace all of sequestration with more responsible deficit reduction that would be better for our national security, long-term economic growth, and our fiscal health.

311.title: Murray Urges Senate GOP Leadership to Stop Blocking Bipartisan Budget Conference
311.description:
Senate Budget Committee Chairman Patty Murray (D-WA) delivered remarks on the Senate floor urging Senate Republican leadership to end their obstruction and allow the House and Senate to move to a bipartisan budget conference. Today marked the 16th time Democrats have requested to go to conference in the 110 days since the Senate passed its budget. Chairman Murray's unanimous consent request was blocked by Senator Rubio.

Chairman Murray described the harmful impacts sequestration is having in Washington state and across the country, especially as defense furloughs go into effect this week, and criticized House Republicans' attempts to stall negotiations and manufacture crises to gain leverage around raising the debt ceiling. Chairman Murray also expressed disappointment at hearing that some Tea Party Republicans want to manufacture a crisis in order to—once again—attempt to defund the Affordable Care Act.

312.title: "I'm Just a Budget" | #conferencenotcrisis
312.description: Today, the Senate Budget Committee majority released an animated web video, "I'm Just a Budget," in which an animated singing budget explains why it's been 100 days since the Senate passed him and he still can't go to conference.

314.description:
Chairman Patty Murray (D-WA) and the Senate Budget Committee held a hearing on the impact federal budget decisions have on our children and long-term economic growth. Majority witnesses included Bruce Lesley, President of First Focus, Margaret Nimmo Crowe, the Acting Executive Director at Voices for Virginia's Children, and Shavon Collier and Sakhia Whitehead, a Head Start parent and local student. 

At the hearing, Chairman Murray highlighted the effect our budget decisions have on our nation's children, and the need to ensure that their voices are heard in the process. Several children attended the hearing, and Sakhia Whitehead, a ten-year-old Head Start graduate, testified and about the positive impact the program had on her education. Her mother, Shavon Collier, spoke about the positive impact federal programs have had on her five children. Bruce Lesley and Margaret Nimmo Crowe shared additional stories about how sequestration is impacting families and children across the country.

315.title: Murray Urges Senate Republican Leadership to Stop Blocking Bipartisan Budget Conference
315.description:
Today, Senate Budget Committee Chairman Patty Murray delivered a speech on the Senate floor urging Senate Republican leadership to stop blocking a bipartisan budget conference and allow the House and Senate to engage in formal negotiations. Chairman Murray asked unanimous consent to move to conference, marking the 14th time Democrats have requested to move to conference in the 88 days since the Senate Budget passed, and was blocked by Senator Pat Toomey (R-PA).   

Murray criticized Senate Republicans' changing excuses for blocking conference, including their recent effort to stall negotiations by focusing on a thirty-year budget outlook. Murray noted that many Senate Republicans have spoken out against their leadership's Tea Party-backed strategy of obstructing a budget conference.

At this hearing, Secretary Arne Duncan testified on the education proposals in the President's Fiscal Year 2014 Budget. Murray asked Duncan to discuss the effects of sequestration and other budget decisions on students, families, and communities, and also questioned Duncan about his specific plans to make sure higher education is affordable with student loan rates set to double on July 1st.

317.title: Senate Budget Committee Hearing | 6.12.13 | Chairman Murray Opening Remarks
